item.title: Red Crescent scales up six-month dengue response
item.description:
A six-month dengue response operation is being scaled up to reach around 300,000 people in areas experiencing high transmission, with vulnerable communities and families being prioritized.
The Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS), with support from the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) and its partners, will implement the operation in Dhaka, Khulna, Barisal and Chittagong, including camps for displaced people from Rakhine State, Myanmar, and host communities in Cox’s Bazar.
The operation may be expanded to other affected areas as the situation evolves.
The initiative comes as dengue cases have increased sharply following heavy monsoon rains in late August.
According to Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) data, 67,367 dengue patients had been hospitalized and 201 deaths had been recorded as of September 23.
During the corresponding period in 2025, more than 43,173 dengue patients had been hospitalized and 184 deaths had been recorded.
“This is a rapidly evolving public health situation, and our volunteers and teams are already supporting communities and coordinating closely with health authorities,” BDRCS Secretary General Md Habibur Rahman Khan said.
“With support from the IFRC and partners, we are strengthening these efforts to reach more people in high-risk areas and help families cope with the health and economic impacts of dengue,” he added.
The BDRCS-IFRC response will complement the government’s ongoing dengue response, led by the DGHS and supported through national and local health coordination mechanisms.
IFRC Head of Delegation in Bangladesh Seval Guzelkilinc said dengue was placing growing pressure on families, communities and health services across Bangladesh.
“While treatment and healthcare support are essential, preventing infections starts at the community level through awareness, early action and efforts to reduce mosquito breeding sites,” she said.
She said: “The strength of the response lies in linking community action with access to timely health services.”
“Through the Bangladesh Red Crescent’s volunteer network and close coordination with health authorities, we can help people protect themselves, access timely support and reduce the impact of dengue on the most vulnerable communities,” she added.
The wider Red Cross and Red Crescent network is also supporting the response. Through existing programs, the IFRC has provided 38,000 NS1 dengue test kits to the DGHS and 50 apheresis kits to the BDRCS Dhaka Blood Centre.
Community engagement and surveillance activities are also ongoing.
Since dengue cases began rising, the BDRCS has supported the national response through community awareness, cleanliness activities, health services and blood centers.
On September 12, it mobilized 1,000 volunteers for the government’s nationwide dengue prevention campaign.

item.title: Yao: Bangladesh-China relations face ever brighter future
item.description:
Chinese Ambassador in Dhaka Yao Wen has voiced firm confidence in an “ever brighter” future for Bangladesh-China relations, saying no challenge could impede the advancement of friendship and cooperation between the two countries.
“The China-Bangladesh friendship serves the fundamental interests of both countries and both peoples and conforms to the trend of the times; no storm can hold back the forward march of our relations,” he said.
The ambassador was addressing a reception in Dhaka on Wednesday evening celebrating the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China.
Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan attended the reception as chief guest.
Ministers, senior political leaders from the ruling and opposition parties, senior government officials, diplomats stationed in Dhaka, business leaders, civil society representatives and senior journalists attended the event.
Yao, who is set to leave Bangladesh early next month after serving here for nearly four years, used the occasion to reflect on the transformation he witnessed in Bangladesh and the evolution of bilateral relations during his tenure.
“Looking back fills me with deep emotion. I have served in Bangladesh for three years and nine months, and I will bid farewell to this post in a few days,” he said.
“As I prepare to leave, my heart is filled with profound attachment and reluctance to part,” the ambassador added.
Yao said he had personally witnessed Bangladesh’s political transformation and what he described as the country’s “historic choices” at a critical juncture.
He expressed admiration for the resilience and national dignity demonstrated by the Bangladeshi people and said the country had embarked on a new path of reform and development under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
The envoy particularly highlighted the potential of Bangladesh’s younger generation.
“Over the past three years, I have walked through the streets and alleys of Dhaka, and what impressed me most is the optimism and drive of Bangladesh’s young people,” he said.
Describing young people as a nation’s “most precious treasure” and its future, Yao said: “I am fully confident in a bright tomorrow of Bangladesh.”
The ambassador said his interactions with Bangladeshis during his tenure had given him a first-hand experience of the friendship between the peoples of the two countries.
“Wherever I went, the warm greetings and sincere smiles made me feel the heartfelt friendship of the Bangladeshi people toward the Chinese people,” he said.
Yao said the friendships he had developed during his posting in Bangladesh would remain with him after his departure.
“May the China-Bangladesh friendship remain evergreen forever! May both our countries enjoy prosperity and our peoples happiness and well-being!” he said.
The ambassador noted that 2026 marks the 51st anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Bangladesh and China as well as the 10th anniversary of bilateral cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative.
The year also marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China, he said.
Yao reiterated Beijing’s support for Bangladesh in safeguarding its national independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity, while opposing external interference and supporting Dhaka in playing a greater role in regional and international affairs.
The ambassador also highlighted Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s first official visit to China since assuming office.
During the June visit, Bangladesh and China agreed to elevate their Comprehensive Strategic Cooperative Partnership and jointly build a “China-Bangladesh Community with a Shared Future in the New Era,” according to the Chinese side.
Yao said the development injected fresh momentum into the long-term advancement of bilateral relations.
Beijing has also said it wants to deepen practical cooperation with Bangladesh in trade and investment, infrastructure, agriculture, the digital economy and green energy while strengthening coordination in regional and international affairs.
“China-Bangladesh relations are now at their best in history,” Yao said, expressing confidence that bilateral friendship and cooperation would continue to broaden in the years ahead.

item.title: Shahe Alam: 4 crore families to get Family Cards, no bribes needed
item.description:
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam has said four crore families will gradually come under the government’s Family Card programme, with no bribes required to obtain the cards.
“Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s government is a government of the people. That is why he has introduced several signature projects for the people, including the Family Card. Four crore families will come under the programme. No one needs to pay a bribe to get the card. Everyone will receive it in phases. Prime Minister’s wife Dr Zubaida Rahman will also receive a Family Card. This is a decision of the BNP government,” he said.
The state minister made the remarks on Thursday afternoon while speaking as the chief guest at a cheque-distribution ceremony organised by the Chittagong District Council at the Baharchhara Union Parishad premises in Banshkhali upazila.
The cheques were distributed as financial assistance for rehabilitating people affected by the recent floods.
Shahe Alam said the BNP would seek votes again by highlighting its tangible development achievements, including improvements in electricity and gas supplies, roads, education and sports, rather than making promises of paradise.
“The BNP government is a government of the people. The government has been in office for only a short time. Short-, medium- and long-term plans have been taken to bring changes in various sectors, including electricity and gas. After five years, we will return to the people and give an account of the government’s work,” he said.
He also said BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia made two Jamaat leaders ministers in 2001 in an attempt to remove the “Razakar” label from them.
“But Jamaat has now forgotten those things,” he said.
On the government’s efforts to rehabilitate flood victims, Shahe Alam said the authorities were making every effort to support those affected.
“People in Banshkhali, Chandanaish and Satkania suffered extensive damage due to sudden heavy rainfall and flooding. The district administration and the government have stood by the people to deal with the situation,” he said.
The state minister apologised to the people for any shortcomings in government assistance. He said additional relief allocations were secured in consultation with the district administration and relevant ministries whenever shortages arose during the floods.
“I came to Banshkhali at the direction of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. He instructed me to stand by the flood victims and take necessary measures,” Shahe Alam said.
On the development of Banshkhali, the state minister said the tender had already been floated to widen the Anwara-Banshkhali-Chakaria road to 34 feet.
“The road project, costing several hundred crore taka, is expected to be completed within the next one to one and a half years. If you provide a list of other roads in Banshkhali that need repair or construction, my ministry will take the necessary steps,” he said.
Urging BNP leaders and activists to remain patient, Shahe Alam said the party had returned to power after a long time and still had much of its government term remaining.
“Those who stood by the party during its difficult times will be evaluated gradually. Within the framework of law and regulations, they will be given opportunities for jobs, legitimate dealerships and government work,” he said.
Speaking as the chair of the programme, Chittagong District Council Administrator Mahabuber Rahman Shamim said the district council had distributed relief among flood-affected people during the floods.
“After taking charge as administrator, I announced that the district council would stand by families affected by the floods and support their rehabilitation. Financial assistance is being provided to 510 families in Banshkhali for rehabilitation. Another 590 families in Chitttgong will receive assistance in phases,” he said.

item.title: Mobile phone, internet revolutionize the poultry industry with free flow of price information
item.description:
Egg farmers in rural areas want to find a trader who will buy at a higher price. Egg traders in each city want to find a supplier who will sell at a lower price. The egg price in each city is determined by the supply of eggs to that city and the demand for eggs in that city. Cellphones have created an information network which empowers thousands of egg producers and traders to compare prices.
The poultry industry has grown as consumption has grown. The Household Income and Expenditure Survey shows that egg consumption per capita increased by 145% between 2005 and 2022, from 5.2 grams to 12.73 grams per person per day. Chicken and duck consumption increased by 285% during the same 17-year period, from 6.8 grams to 26.17 grams per person per day. This rapid growth shows clearly that there is no cartel which is limiting supply. New companies and farmers enter the poultry business whenever prices are high, showing that there is no barrier to entry. Economists say that a cartel (or “syndicate”) is not possible in a business where there is no barrier to entry.
Industry stakeholders say that it is not possible for producers or traders to form a cartel, because there are thousands of people buying and selling eggs every day, and information about the market price in each place is easy to obtain over via mobile phone. If anyone tries to sell at a high price, no one will buy from him.
The recent increase in egg price is attributed to a fall in egg production during hot summer months, and because many marginal egg farmers sold their hens (and stopped producing eggs) during the recent months of low egg prices (January to May 2026).
Dr Sabbir Hossain (28) is a veterinarian and farmer with 3,500 layer hens of Horipur village in Ghatail, Tangail. He said, "I know the price of eggs everywhere. The arotdars (wholesalers) who buy eggs from us cannot fix the price, and neither can we. In fact, there is no centre where the price is fixed." He said that information technology allows poultry farmers to get information about prices. On 17 September, he sold eggs for Tk 11 per egg, and made a profit. He made losses for many months when the price was low.
Nazrul Islam (52) is a small farmer in Luchia Nagarbari, Madhupur. He said that farmers like him sell eggs to whoever offers a higher price. "Because of mobile phones with internet, we can check the market price anytime." he said.
Jahangir Khan (42), runs Noor Dimer Arot (wholesale shop) at Pakutia, Ghatail. He buys about 20,000 eggs each day from farmers and small traders and sells them to wholesalers in Moulvibazar and Dhaka. "In the morning I get an idea of the day’s price, and then call farmers and traders to offer a price," he said. He explained that when demand increases in Dhaka and other cities, egg prices also increase in rural markets. "Farmers can sell at a better price because they can get market information via mobile."
Keramot Ali Khan (48), is one of the owners of Setu Enterprise in Porabari, Ghatail. He sells up to 100,000 eggs almost every day to wholesale traders in Kaptanbazar, Dhaka. "I buy mostly from traders in Tangail and Jamalpur districts. Whether I am buying or selling, the price depends on demand and supply," he said.
Currently about 2 million eggs are traded each day at Tejgaon, a small fraction of the 15 million eggs sold in Dhaka city each day. National production of commercial eggs is estimated at about 50 million eggs per day. Amanat Ullah, a leader of the Egg Traders Multipurpose Samity (association) told this author that “The price depends on supply and demand, it can’t be influenced by anyone.”
Kazi Farms auctions about 700,000 eggs each day at its sales centre in Ashulia near Dhaka city. According to Kazi Zahin Hasan, director of Kazi Farms, “We try to sell our entire stock of eggs each day, because eggs are perishable . Every morning, buyers submit their price bids and their desired quantity of eggs through our phone app. We examine the bids, and determine the highest price at which all our eggs will be sold. If we want to sell 700,000 eggs, and each bidder wants about 50,000 eggs, we only need to sell eggs to the 14 highest bidders. So our selling price will be the 14 th highest price bid. We will sell to all of the 14 highest bidders at the same price, so they all feel that they are treated fairly. Economists call this a commodity auction with a uniform selling price, many buyers and sealed bids. Our customers have the option of buying from other sellers. They are buying from us because our price is competitive compared to other sellers. At present, the demand for eggs exceeds the supply, and our auction price is higher than it was a few months ago. In February, when the supply of eggs exceeded the demand, our auction price was only 7.43 Taka per egg. Every egg producer made losses for about five months this year. When demand is higher than supply, the price is high, and consumers are unhappy, but farmers make profit. When supply is higher than demand, the price is low, and consumers are happy, but farmers lose money. Prices of agricultural products like eggs and vegetables are never stable.”

item.title: UN rights chief ‘appalled’ by Yemen conflict’s swelling civilian toll
item.description:
The UN rights chief voiced outrage Thursday at the growing civilian toll in Yemen, as the conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces and their allies intensifies.
The recent Houthi takeover of Yemen’s Red Sea coast has left hundreds dead and heightened fears over global trade and shipping through the vital Bab al-Mandab strait.
It has also forced thousands to flee, with the United Nations on Tuesday forecasting the number of displaced could swell from over 130,000 today to more than 230,000 in the coming months.
UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said he was “appalled” at the situation.
“As if the people of Yemen haven’t already endured enough misery, civilians are now bearing the brunt of this latest upsurge in fighting,” he said in a statement, insisting that “civilians must never be targeted, and their protection must be the overriding priority.”
Turk’s office said at least 125 civilians had been killed or injured in Houthi attacks since the start of August, adding that it had documented the killings of 32 of those civilians, including 15 children and three women.
It also said it had documented three Houthi attacks on sites hosting internally displaced people in Marib province on August 7 and September 9.
The Houthis meanwhile say Saudi Arabia has conducted hundreds of strikes in Yemen since the collapse of a four-year truce in July.
“Warring parties must distinguish at all times between civilians and combatants and between civilian objects and military objectives,” Turk said.
The UN rights chief also stressed that warnings or designations of so-called “kill-zones”, which he said had recently been declared by the Yemeni government, do not “remove the protection afforded to civilians and civilian objects.”
Turk called on all sides in the conflict to allow and facilitate humanitarian aid to reach civilians in need.
“People fleeing the fighting, as well as those already displaced, must be protected and have safe access to food, water, shelter, healthcare and other essential services,” he said, urging all sides to “step back from further escalation.”
“The people of Yemen cannot withstand another full-scale conflict.”

item.title: Trump to fete Xi with lavish White House welcome
item.description:
US President Donald Trump will host Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the White House on Thursday for a day full of pageantry with one goal -- keeping the fragile peace between the rival superpowers.
Trump personally greeted Xi on the tarmac after his arrival on Wednesday, the first time in more than six decades that a US president has welcomed a foreign political leader at Joint Base Andrews near Washington.
He will lay on more pomp and ceremony for Xi on Thursday, treating him to a formal welcome on the White House South Lawn, a military flyover, talks in the Oval Office and finally a grand state banquet.
But the lavish welcome masks deep tensions over thorny topics including the trade war between the world’s top two economies, artificial intelligence and Beijing’s diplomatic and economic support for Iran.
Xi urged cooperation in comments reported by Chinese state media shortly after his arrival, saying that China and the United States should be “partners rather than rivals.”
The Chinese president added that he was looking “forward to in-depth exchanges with President Trump on major issues concerning our bilateral relations and the global situation.”
An early piece of good news for Beijing and Washington was the announcement by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Wednesday of a two-month extension of a trade truce that was due to expire in November.
Both sides are keen to avoid plunging back into the trade war sparked by the US president’s sweeping global tariffs last year.
But while Trump boasts that he will get results from what he calls his “great relationship” with Xi -- the latest in a series of authoritarian leaders he has befriended -- few breakthroughs are expected.
Instead their third meeting since Trump returned to power is aimed at maintaining the broader detente despite the underlying tensions.
Xi’s first White House state visit in more than a decade will therefore be more about spectacle than substance.
The program includes a military inspection in the Rose Garden -- which Trump recently paved over -- and a gift-giving ceremony involving Trump’s wife Melania and Xi’s wife Peng Liyuan.
Trump and Xi will make remarks in the morning and again in the evening, though it remains unclear if there will be an opportunity for reporters to put questions to the two leaders.
The state dinner will feature a host of top US tech and AI company bosses -- although Xi’s delegation includes no CEOs, sources told AFP.
Trump set the tone on Wednesday when he and Melania met the Chinese presidential couple on a red carpet at Joint Base Andrews, before a military band played the national anthems and US bombers flew noisily overhead.
“I thought it was a great little meeting, a great greeting, and I think they appreciate it,” Trump told reporters -- brushing off the fact that Xi had not welcomed him at the airport for his Beijing state visit in May.
Trump confirmed that his stalled Iran war would be on the agenda, despite earlier playing down reports that Beijing was giving Tehran intelligence.
“I’ll be talking about that and many other subjects -- but it’s all coming along well, including that,” Trump said.
Artificial intelligence is also set to dominate the summit amid growing fears that it risks wiping out humanity -- even as China and the United States race for supremacy in the field.
Taiwan will also be on the cards, with Trump’s words likely to be watched for any sign of diminishing US support for the self-governing island that Beijing claims as its territory.
Xi’s visit will wrap up on Friday morning when the two presidential couples have tea at the White House and then visit the National Archives, home to the US Declaration of Independence.

item.title: US judge blocks White House ban on CNN, MS NOW, Politico
item.description:
The Trump administration must immediately reinstate White House access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico, a US federal judge ordered Thursday, after their reporters were banned from the premises.
President Donald Trump has long attacked media outlets that have aired critical coverage of his campaigns and administrations, repeatedly blasting the press as the “enemy of the people.”
The three outlets were barred from the White House by the billionaire former reality TV star on Friday as punishment for distributing what he branded “fake news” and “fiction and lies.”
Theodore Boutrous, who is representing the media outlets, told AFP on Thursday that “this is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law. We greatly appreciate the court’s swift action.”
CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a joint lawsuit asking for a temporary restraining order against the ban on the grounds that it violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which upholds the right to a free press.
Judge Timothy Kelly found that the revocation of press passes “likely violated their constitutional due process rights,” according to the eight-page ruling issued Thursday.
“The ‘general rule’ is that ‘individuals must receive notice and an opportunity to be heard before the Government deprives them’ of a constitutionally protected interest,” Kelly wrote.
The judge said that press credentials held by employees of the three outlets will be reinstated “until further Order of the Court or the expiration of this Temporary Restraining Order,” which is to remain in effect for 14 days.
Kelly added that the order cannot be immediately appealed.
AFP has contacted the Department of Justice for comment.
Ahead of the ruling, the Department of Justice had argued Trump can “control reporters’ access to restricted presidential areas, such as the Oval Office.”
“Access to the White House is a privilege -- not a right,” it said.
The White House Press Office accused CNN in a letter to the cable news outlet of “trafficking in verifiable falsehoods about national security and other issues, and publishing sensitive or classified information,” with similar accusations leveled against MS NOW and Politico.
The letter to CNN cited several stories about the US-Iran war and a story on Trump’s plans to build a military bunker below the planned East Wing ballroom which allegedly “disclosed ‘top-secret’ construction details.”
Boutrous told the judge on Wednesday that in Trump’s Truth Social post announcing the bans, the president “didn’t say anything about national security.”
The lawyer argued that being punished for reporting on national security issues “that the government would rather have not be reported on is just contrary to First Amendment principles.”
Kelly said the stories identified in letters to the outlets were “routine.”
“The Court is skeptical -- at least on this record -- that Defendants’ interest in safeguarding national security is the actual motivation for, or is even advanced by, the revocation of Plaintiffs’ hard passes,” Kelly said, referring to the White House press credentials.
Journalists for the three news organizations were denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday and had their passes confiscated, in the latest flare-up of the 80-year-old Republican president’s assault on mainstream US media.
In a previous case involving CNN during Trump’s first term, Kelly, a Trump appointee, ordered the White House to temporarily restore access for a CNN reporter whose pass had been revoked.
In a rare move, the top five US broadcasters said Monday that they were halting pool coverage of the White House -- where a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the day -- in solidarity with CNN.
“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting,” ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC said.
The White House Correspondents’ Association and nearly 50 news organizations also filed a brief with the court calling for the bans on CNN, MS NOW and Politico to be reversed.
Trump appeared to suggest on Tuesday that CNN should not be covering him outside of the White House either.
“I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me. You shouldn’t be here,” Trump told a reporter at the UN General Assembly in New York.
The White House launched a streaming channel, Trump TV, on Monday which it said would show “top videos, major remarks, and must-see highlights streaming 24/7 and updated in real time.”
The ban came at a time when Trump’s approval ratings are at record lows, his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in November’s midterm elections, and the Middle East conflict drags on with no end in sight.

item.title: Biman signs deal to buy 11 more Boeing aircraft
item.description:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has signed an agreement with US aircraft manufacturer Boeing to buy 11 more aircraft as Bangladesh moves to expand its aviation sector and open new routes, Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin said on Wednesday.
“A significant signing ceremony was held with Boeing today [Wednesday], where Biman Bangladesh Airlines signed an agreement to purchase 11 more Boeing aircraft,” he said at a press briefing at the Hyatt Grand Central New York.
Mahdi said Biman Chairman Rumee A Hossain signed the agreement on behalf of the national flag carrier.
He said Bangladesh is buying aircraft based on its own requirements as the aviation sector is expanding. “We buy aircraft based on our needs. We want to expand our aviation sector, and for that we need aircraft,” he said.
The adviser said Bangladesh has a long-standing commercial relationship with Boeing, while discussions with Airbus could also take place based on the country’s requirements.
“The two companies that provide good aircraft are Boeing and Airbus. We will buy from Boeing or Airbus according to our needs. No one will force us to buy either,” he said.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said the signing ceremony was significant as several senior US government officials attended the event.
US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, Under Secretary of Commerce William Kimmitt, Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Paul Kapur and Special Representative for Commercial and Business Affairs Vinay Chawla attended the ceremony.
Kobir said the presence of the senior US officials demonstrated the importance of Bangladesh-US relations.
He said the participation of senior officials from the US Commerce and State Departments showed that the two countries are looking at expanding trade and investment while strengthening bilateral relations.
Referring to President Donald Trump’s recent letter to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, the state minister said the US President had expressed his appreciation for Bangladesh’s decision to purchase Boeing aircraft and conveyed confidence in the country’s future under Tarique Rahman’s leadership.
He said the Boeing agreement was also important from the perspective of expanding Bangladesh’s aviation sector and strengthening economic ties with the United States.
Mahdi said the Boeing delegation later held a courtesy meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
In April, Bangladesh signed a deal with Boeing to purchase 14 aircraft for Biman in a deal valued at $3.7 billion, described as the airline’s biggest-ever aircraft order.
In a letter to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on September 1, Trump thanked him for the decision to purchase Boeing aircraft and said Boeing would not let Bangladesh down.
Mahdi said technical assessments and discussions were also underway on possible future aircraft purchases, including from Airbus, based on Bangladesh’s requirements.
He said Bangladesh is expanding its aviation sector, planning new routes and will need additional aircraft to meet growing demand.
Kobir said Bangladesh will continue to assess its requirements before making further aircraft purchases, adding that the government wants to ensure that its aviation expansion serves the country’s interests.
The Boeing signing was among a series of activities during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s four-day visit to New York to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
The signing ceremony was attended by Brad McMullen, Boeing senior vice president of Commercial Sales and Marketing, and Rumee A Hossain, chairman of Biman Bangladesh Airlines, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat, Kobir, Mahdi, Invest Bangladesh Authority Chairman Chowdhury Ashik Mahmud Bin Harun, Howard Lutnick and Christopher Landau on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

item.title: UNGA81: PM calls for urgent global action on climate crisis, predictable finance
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday called for five urgent global actions to tackle climate change and ensure a just and equitable transition, including meeting the 1.5°C target and ensuring predictable climate finance.
“Collective action based on “Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities” is imperative…We call for 5 urgent actions,” he said.
Tarique made the call while addressing a high-level meeting on “Climate Action and the Just Transition” at the UN Headquarters in New York.
Outlining the five urgent actions, the Prime Minister first called for achieving the 1.5°C global warming limit through global emission cuts, as set out in the Paris Agreement.
Second, Tarique called for predictable and accessible finance for adaptation in climate-vulnerable countries.
Third, he urged greater access to climate-smart technologies to enable a just and equitable climate transition.
Fourth, Tarique stressed the need for expanding renewable energy through accessible finance, capacity-building and technology transfer.
And fifth, he called for full implementation and regular replenishment of the Loss and Damage Fund.
“Bangladesh seeks partnerships that help us implement our plans. Let us act together to build a safer and more sustainable future for generations to come,” the Prime Minister added.
Tarique said Bangladesh contributes less than 0.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions but is among the most climate-vulnerable countries.
He said Bangladesh could lose 12 to 18% of its coastal areas to sea-level rise by the end of this century, affecting the livelihoods of tens of millions of people.
“Climate change has caused loss and damage equivalent to 1% of our GDP. Our food security is at serious risk,” Tarique said.
The prime minister said Bangladesh had allocated nearly $3.19 billion in its budget for climate adaptation but warned that the country risked severe damage without international support.
He said Bangladesh plans to plant 250 million trees over five years and dig around 20,000 kilometres of rivers and canals, alongside the Padma Barrage and Teesta Barrage Master Plan, to retain water, reduce flood risks, revive wetlands and recharge groundwater.
The government also aims to generate 20% of the country's electricity demand from renewable sources by 2030, Tarique said.
Bangladesh is promoting green industries, including jute products, eco-friendly transport, waste-to-energy and circular economy initiatives, while developing a national carbon market, he said adding that, “But we cannot succeed in isolation.”
The high-level meeting was held at the Trusteeship Council Chamber of the UN Headquarters as part of the Prime Minister's engagements during the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.

item.title: Ajmul murder: Asif claims video recorded of forced confession
item.description:
A newly arrested suspect in the Ajmul murder case has told the Special Response Battalion (SRB) that the victim was tortured and forced to confess to stealing rice, a mobile phone and money, with a video recorded during the interrogation.
Sheikh Asif Hossain, a former Khulna University student, also told SRB-6 that Ajmul fell to the ground after slipping while attempting to jump from the fourth-floor roof to the third floor to escape those assaulting him, according to the battalion.
SRB-6 Commander Lt Col Nistar Ahmed said Asif was arrested in Bhatiyapara, Gopalganj. He is the son of Sheikh Miraj of Sanatankati village in Paikgacha upazila, Khulna.
After preliminary interrogation, Asif was handed over to Harintana police station under Khulna Metropolitan Police for further legal action.
According to the SRB commander, Asif had secured a job at a private bank and was scheduled to join on September 20, but went into hiding after Ajmul’s death on the night of September 18.
During interrogation, Asif said he had gone to the building on Friday night to meet classmates from his university batch. He was present when Ajmul was allegedly beaten inside a room.
He said Ajmul was later taken to the fourth-floor roof and assaulted. Those present allegedly tried to force him to confess to stealing rice, a mobile phone and money, while several people recorded videos of his statements.
According to Asif’s account, Ajmul was subsequently threatened with being handed over to police. Fearing arrest, Ajmul attempted to jump from the fourth floor to the third floor but slipped and fell to the ground, sustaining serious injuries. He later died after being taken to hospital.
Asif also told the SRB that mess manager Mehedi and Habib Hasnat Rifat, a cash officer at Krishi Bank’s Town Noapara branch, were directly involved in the incident. He alleged that Rifat played a significant role in beating Ajmul, but said there was no intention to kill him.
He also identified Tarek, alias Rubel, owner of Ma-Babar Doa Tanha Juice Corner in front of Khaja Hall, as another person who physically assaulted Ajmul.
Harintana police station Officer-in-Charge Md Iqbal Hossain said four people have been arrested in connection with the case since the night of September 18.
The arrested suspects include three former Khulna University students and a juice shop owner, he said.
Iqbal said Rifat gave a confessional statement before a court under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on September 22, followed by Pratap and Rubel on September 23.
He said the suspects provided information during police interrogation, which is being reviewed and verified. Asif is scheduled to be produced before a court on September 24 and may also give a voluntary statement.
The OC said further information could emerge if mess manager Mehedi is arrested.
Ajmul, a first-year English student at North Western University, was allegedly beaten at a four-storey building on Islamnagar Road, near Khulna University’s Hall Road, on the night of September 18 over allegations of stealing rice.
He subsequently fell from the building and died. His relatives have alleged that he was beaten to death.
On September 19, Ajmul’s father, Kutubuddin, filed a murder case with Harintana police station, naming four Khulna University students and accusing 20-25 unidentified people.
Four people have so far been arrested in connection with the case.

item.title: Dhaka records ‘moderate’ air quality Thursday morning
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 37th among the world's most polluted cities on Thursday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 64 at 10:22am.
The air quality was classified as "moderate", indicating that the air quality is generally acceptable, although unusually sensitive people may experience some health effects, according to the AQI scale.
DR Congo’s Kinshasa topped the list with an AQI score of 239.
Malaysia’s Kuching and Pakistan’s Lahore jointly ranked second, with AQI scores of 194 each.
Dubai, United Arab Emirates, ranked third, with an AQI score of 157.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Education Minister: Govt plans specialised university on blue economy
item.description:
The government is working on the blue economy and plans to establish a specialised university focusing on the sector in the future, Education Minister Dr A N M Ehsanul Hoque Milon said on Wednesday.
He made the remarks while addressing a scholarship distribution ceremony organised jointly by the Marketing Alumni Association of Dhaka University and Meghna Group of Industries (MGI) at the Nabab Nawab Ali Chowdhury Senate Building.
The minister said the government is working to develop Bangladesh’s human resources by equipping them with the skills needed for the future.
“The government is working with the highest priority on the education sector to improve the country’s education system,” he said.
Highlighting the importance of exposure to diverse cultures and experiences, Milon said such exposure enables people to analyse problems from multiple perspectives.
He urged students not to confine themselves to a single field but to apply their knowledge, talents and skills across different areas.
Speaking about the gap between academia and industry, the education minister said major companies and industries in Bangladesh do not give sufficient importance to strengthening linkages between the two sectors.
“It is unfortunate that big companies and industries in our country do not attach enough importance to academia-industry linkage,” he said.
Referring to China, he said industries there have established polytechnic institutes within industrial facilities, allowing engineers to teach students while students gain practical experience by working in those industries. “Such a linkage is also necessary in our country,” he added.
“The people before me today will build the Bangladesh of tomorrow. Our intellect is in no way inferior to that of citizens of other countries,” he said addressing the students.
Milon praised MGI’s corporate social responsibility initiative of providing scholarships to university students and urged other corporate organizations to come forward with similar initiatives to support education.
The event, titled ‘MGI-MAA Scholarship 2026,’ was organised jointly by MGI and the DU Marketing Department Alumni Association to provide scholarships to 90 students of the Marketing Department of DU.

item.title: Six decades on, Dinajpur BSCIC still struggles with basic services
item.description:
Despite more than six decades of operation and Tk 225.50 crore in investment, the BSCIC Industrial Estate in Dinajpur is still struggling to provide basic infrastructure and services to its entrepreneurs.
Established in 1962, the industrial estate has generated employment for nearly 4,825 people. Yet it continues to face longstanding problems, including the absence of a boundary wall, inadequate drainage, poor waste management and waterlogging during the rainy season.
Entrepreneurs say the lack of essential facilities is disrupting industrial operations and discouraging new investment in the estate.
The Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industries Corporation (BSCIC) established the industrial estate on 35.14 acres of land in the Pulhat area of Dinajpur town in 1962 at a cost of Tk 45.54 lakh. The project was completed in 1972.
Initially, 189 industrial plots were allocated, covering 28.74 acres. According to BSCIC data, 54 industrial units are currently located in the estate, of which 52 are operational. Two units—M/s Habiba Aluminium Industries (Pvt.) Ltd and M/s Rupon Oil and Feeds (Pvt.) Ltd—are closed due to bank loan defaults, with related cases pending in court.
The estate houses a diverse range of industries, including food processing, rice milling, engineering, chemical, timber, bakery, silver, automated flour milling, pulse and edible oil processing.
There are 33 A-type plots measuring 15,000 square feet each, 42 B-type plots of 9,000 square feet, 64 C-type plots of 4,500 square feet and 65 D-type plots of 2,250 square feet.
BSCIC data show that the industrial units have created employment for around 4,825 workers and employees, including 3,377 men and 1,448 women. Total investment stands at Tk 225.50 crore, while the annual value of production is Tk 302.58 crore.
The industrial estate generates Tk 201.54 lakh in annual government revenue from various sources. This includes Tk 165 lakh in income tax and VAT, Tk 1.35 lakh from electricity, Tk 4.26 lakh in land development tax, Tk 0.90 lakh in municipal tax, Tk 30 lakh in service charges and transfer fees, and Tk 0.03 lakh from telephone services.
The absence of a boundary wall has raised security concerns, while the inadequate drainage system causes waterlogging during the rainy season. The stagnant water makes movement difficult for workers and hampers the transportation of raw materials and finished goods.
Entrepreneurs have also complained about the accumulation of garbage in and around the industrial area, saying inadequate infrastructure and services are increasing their operating costs.
They said they pay an annual service charge of Tk 3.50 per square foot. Including VAT and land-related charges, the total comes to Tk 4.31 per square foot. Despite paying the charges regularly, they alleged that the services provided by the authorities do not meet their needs.
Md Nuruzzaman Sarker, president of the Dinajpur Rice Mill Owners' Group, called for immediate measures to improve the drainage system, construct a boundary wall and strengthen security at the estate.
Md Abu Bakar Siddiq, president of the Dinajpur Chamber of Commerce and Industry and owner of an auto-rice mill, said service charges are increasing every year, while the quality of services remains inadequate.
“New entrepreneurs are losing interest as a result. New investment cannot be encouraged without proper services and government support,” he said.
BSCIC officials, however, said they have taken initiatives to address the problems.
Md Jahedul Islam, deputy general manager of Dinajpur BSCIC, acknowledged the shortcomings, including the lack of a boundary wall and problems with roads, drainage and waste management.
He said the industrial estate requires renovation and that a cost estimate for constructing a boundary wall had been submitted to the BSCIC headquarters for allocation in the 2025–26 fiscal year.
“Once the allocation is received, steps will be taken to construct the boundary wall and resolve the other problems,” he said.
Entrepreneurs and business leaders are now questioning why basic infrastructure and service deficiencies have persisted for more than six decades despite substantial investment, production and employment at the estate.
They said timely improvements to infrastructure and services could help Dinajpur BSCIC attract new industries, retain existing businesses and create more employment opportunities.

item.title: HRW: Three laws weaken human rights safeguards in Bangladesh
item.description:
Three laws passed by parliament in September have weakened human rights protections and backtracked on reform commitments made by the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), Human Rights Watch (HRW) said Tuesday.
According to HRW, the legislation removes safeguards introduced by the interim government, which governed Bangladesh from August 2024 to February 2026, potentially weakening protections against abuses such as enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings.
The interim government had introduced two ordinances aimed at strengthening the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), including by giving it powers to prevent and investigate enforced disappearances and seek accountability.
After being elected earlier this year, the government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has legislated to reduce the NHRC’s independence and investigative powers, HRW said.
The third law, the Special Response Battalion Act, formally abolishes the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establishes the Special Response Battalion (SRB). HRW said the law effectively renames the force while providing fewer safeguards than those applicable to regular police.
“To prevent a return to the terrible abuses of the past, Bangladesh needs real security sector reform and an independent human rights body with the authority to investigate allegations of abuse,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at HRW.
“The new government’s efforts to shield security forces from scrutiny and accountability offer no reason to trust that killings and disappearances will remain a thing of the past,” she said.
Under the Awami League government of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, which ruled Bangladesh from 2009 to 2024, law enforcement agencies committed widespread abuses, including extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, arbitrary arrests of critics and excessive use of force against protesters, according to HRW.
Although killings and disappearances have declined sharply, HRW said the BNP government, like its predecessor, is holding hundreds of perceived political opponents in arbitrary detention.
The Awami League established the NHRC in 2009, but the commission lacked independence and had no authority to investigate allegations against security agencies, HRW said.
Under the previous law, a committee dominated by government or government-aligned officials selected the commissioners. When allegations were made against law enforcement agencies, the NHRC could only seek a report from the government and make recommendations.
The interim government introduced an ordinance to strengthen the commission by empowering it to investigate security agencies, creating a more independent appointments process and providing greater independence in funding and staffing.
The ordinance also established a National Preventive Mechanism to inspect and monitor places of detention, as required under the Optional Protocol to the Convention against Torture.
However, the ordinance needed parliamentary confirmation after the February election or it would automatically lapse.
HRW said the BNP government allowed the ordinance to lapse. A new law passed on September 6, following a walkout by opposition lawmakers, does not allow the NHRC to directly investigate alleged rights violations by security forces.
Instead, the commission can request a report from the agency accused of the violation. HRW said a vaguely worded provision appears to allow the NHRC to initiate its own inquiry if the agency fails to respond or provides an unsatisfactory report.
The law also restores government control over the appointments process, reduces the commission’s budgetary and administrative independence, and weakens the status and independence of the National Preventive Mechanism.
HRW said the new law does not appear to meet the Paris Principles, the international standards for national human rights institutions, in terms of investigative powers, political independence and adequate resources.
Parliament also passed the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act on September 6, reversing reforms introduced by an interim government ordinance, according to HRW.
While the previous ordinance empowered the NHRC to investigate allegations of enforced disappearance, the new law requires the government to appoint a security agency other than the one implicated to investigate such allegations.
The new law also removes the NHRC’s authority to monitor, inspect and investigate detention facilities, including suspected secret detention sites, HRW said.
The legal standard for command responsibility in enforced disappearance cases has also been changed.
Previously based on the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, the standard held commanders responsible for violations they should have known about and prevented. The new law requires evidence of direct orders to hold a commanding officer responsible for an enforced disappearance, according to HRW.
On September 10, parliament passed the Special Response Battalion Act, renaming RAB as the Special Response Battalion (SRB).
RAB has previously been sanctioned by the United States over allegations of serious human rights abuses. Seven former senior officers have been placed under targeted US sanctions, while several former members are facing trial at Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal over alleged crimes against humanity, including enforced disappearance.
The BNP had previously called for RAB’s dissolution.
Under the new law, RAB personnel, powers and property, including records, have been transferred to the SRB, which began operating on September 16, HRW said.
The organisation’s logo has also remained the same, with only the letters “RAB” replaced by “SRB,” according to the rights group.
In May, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said renaming the unit could lead the United States to reconsider sanctions against it.
Human rights experts have criticised the new law for what they say is a lack of safeguards, training, oversight and accountability.
HRW urged Bangladesh’s international partners to press the government to ensure that rules for the SRB include rigorous human rights vetting of personnel, independent external oversight, safeguards governing arrest and detention, preservation of RAB records and other evidence, and an end to the routine deployment of military personnel for civilian law enforcement.
The rights group also called on the United States to maintain sanctions on the renamed entity until adequate measures for human rights protection and accountability for past violations are in place.
It urged international partners, including the European Union and the United Kingdom, to express concern over what it described as the emerging human rights record and policies of the new government.
“Tarique Rahman came to office promising reform, after protesters risked their lives to overthrow a government that had committed widespread and severe rights violations,” Pearson said.
“It is deeply alarming to see the new government so quickly following in the abusive footsteps of Sheikh Hasina, because we have seen where this can lead,” she said.

Cuet students continue shutdown over VC replacement
item.description:
Students at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (Cuet) are observing a second consecutive day of an all-out shutdown and mass signature campaign protesting the decision to replace Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem just 56 days after he assumed office.
Students closed the university’s main gate from inside on Wednesday morning and began the shutdown and mass signature campaign. They have been protesting the decision since Monday night.
On Tuesday, alongside the shutdown, leaders of the Cuet Teachers’ Association formed a human chain in front of the vice-chancellor’s residence, demanding his reinstatement.
No classes or examinations were held at Cuet on Wednesday due to the protests. Administrative activities also remained suspended as the administrative building was locked.
Students have been chanting slogans demanding the reinstatement of Professor Sayem, who assumed office on July 27.
In a press release issued by the students on Tuesday, they said they learned on the evening of Monday that the Ministry of Education’s Secondary and Higher Education Division had appointed Professor Dr Sheikh Shariful Alam, a professor in the Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering Department at Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET), as Cuet’s new vice-chancellor.
The same notification announced the decision to replace Professor Sayem.
The students said they had announced an all-out shutdown and mass sit-in to protest the decision and would continue their movement until Sayem was reinstated.
They also said the notification did not mention any reason for the change.
According to the students, Professor Sayem had gained their confidence within a short period by communicating directly with students, listening to their problems and taking prompt initiatives on academic and administrative matters.
After news of the appointment of the new vice-chancellor spread, students began a protest procession from Swadhinata Chattar on campus around 10:30pm on Monday.
The procession passed through various academic buildings, residential halls and the teachers’ residential area. Around 11pm, female students from different halls also joined the procession.
The students later locked the administrative building. A white paper attached to the lock read: “Only Sayem Sir can open this lock.”
Meanwhile, students have been observing the all-out shutdown and mass signature campaign since Wednesday morning.
“Our Vice-Chancellor Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem sir has been removed after only 56 days. He is a qualified and student-friendly vice-chancellor. We want him reinstated. The movement will continue until a decision is made to reinstate him,” a protesting student said.
Farhan Hasnat Adib, a third-year student of the Department of Mechanical Engineering who took part in the mass signature campaign, said Sayem was removed from the vice-chancellor’s post without prior notice on September 21.
“We held a protest procession on Monday night in response. Yesterday, Tuesday, we observed a complete shutdown at Cuet. Today, on the second day of our movement, we are holding a mass signature campaign, which we will submit to the higher authorities. Our peaceful movement will continue until our demands are met,” he said.
Cuet Director of Student Welfare Professor Saiful Islam said: “The students did not attend classes. Therefore, it was not possible to begin any academic activities.”

item.title: ADB approves $200m loan to modernise power grid
item.description:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a $200 million loan to help Bangladesh modernise and strengthen its power distribution network in peri-urban areas surrounding Dhaka, improving the reliability, efficiency and resilience of electricity supply for businesses and households.
The Power Distribution Network Enhancement Project will support the Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board (BREB) in upgrading electricity distribution infrastructure across 13 Palli Bidyut Samities (PBSs)—or electric cooperatives—serving rapidly growing industrial and urban areas around Dhaka, it said.
Under the ADB-supported Integrated Growth Network Development initiative, the project will help address overloaded substations, ageing infrastructure, power losses, and increasing natural hazard risks that constrain electric service delivery.
“As Bangladesh advances its vision of becoming a more prosperous, resilient, and globally competitive economy, modern power distribution networks will be essential to sustaining growth, creating more jobs, and attracting investment,” said ADB Country Director for Bangladesh Qingfeng Zhang.
“This project will help future-proof the power system in key growth corridors around Dhaka through advanced technologies, stronger infrastructure, and enhanced resilience measures, ensuring that businesses and communities have the reliable electricity they need to thrive,” he said.
The project will install 1,150 megavolt-amperes of new transformer capacity across 52 substations and increase the capacity of 12 existing substations by 115 megavolt-amperes.
It will also construct or upgrade more than 2,600 kilometres of overhead and underground distribution lines and install insulated conductors to improve network reliability, efficiency, and safety.
To modernise system operations, the project will build river-crossing transmission structures and switching stations and deploy 900 fault locator sets for faster fault detection and service restoration.
Bangladesh achieved universal electrification in 2022, but rising electricity demand driven by rapid urbanisation and industrial growth continues to increase pressure on the power network, said an ADB press release.
The project will help strengthen the distribution system’s ability to meet growing demand while supporting the country’s natural hazard-resilient and low-carbon development goals.
ADB’s dedicated resilience financing for the project amounts to $146.52 million, including support for adaptation tools such as an environment-friendly gas-insulated switchgear technology, cutting annual greenhouse gas emissions by about 203,751 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent through improved distribution efficiency and reduced technical losses.
The project will strengthen the institutional capacity of BREB and PBSs through training in digital system integration, cybersecurity, natural hazard-resilient operations, environmental and social safeguards, and financial management.
By strengthening the financial sustainability of PBSs, it will help attract greater private sector participation and investments. The project will also promote practices responsive to the needs of women and girls, including measures to boost women’s participation in the power sector and improve workplace conditions.
ADB’s assistance is complemented by $107.95 million in cofinancing from the Government of Bangladesh and $141.39 million from BREB.
A $1 million technical assistance grant from the Republic of Korea e-Asia and Knowledge Partnership Fund, administered by ADB, will support institutional development, financial sustainability planning, and implementation of innovative technologies.

item.title: Metro services suspended for 26 mins after door opens mid-journey
item.description:
Metro rail services on Dhaka’s Uttara-Motijheel route were suspended for around 26 minutes on Wednesday after a train door suddenly opened while the train was in motion.
Services resumed after the technical fault was repaired.
The incident occurred at around 7:37am on Wednesday.
Train services resumed at 8:03am after the necessary repairs, MRT Police (Operations) Inspector Md Mohsin Sheikh confirmed.
He said a door at the rear section of a metro rail train travelling from Uttara North station towards Motijheel suddenly opened while the train was in motion.
As soon as the issue was noticed, train operations were temporarily suspended to ensure the safety of passengers, he said
Metro rail services on the Uttara-Motijheel route are currently operating normally, authorities said.

item.title: Govt approves import of 155,000 tons of fertilizer from 3 countries
item.description:
The Cabinet Committee on Government Purchase has approved four proposals to import 155,000 tons of fertilizer from Canada, Russia and Saudi Arabia under state-level and government-to-government (G2G) arrangements at a total cost of Tk982.61 crore.
The imports comprise 115,000 tons of Muriate of Potash (MOP) from Canada and Russia and 40,000 tons of diammonium phosphate (DAP) from Saudi Arabia.
Of the MOP, 80,000 tons will be imported from Canada in two lots at a cost of Tk379.35 crore, while 35,000 tons will be imported from Russia for Tk165.90 crore.
The 40,000 tons of DAP from Saudi Arabia will cost Tk437.37 crore.
The proposals from the Ministry of Agriculture were approved at a committee meeting at the Secretariat on Wednesday, chaired by Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury.
The Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) will implement the imports, with the costs covered by the agricultural subsidy budget.

item.title: South Africa: 11 killed in attack on house party
item.description:
Gunmen killed 11 people at a home in eastern South Africa, Kwa-Zulu Natal province’s premier said on Wednesday.
Three people were injured in the attack.
The motive for the shooting was not immediately clear.
The shooting occurred in KwaMakhutha, a township some 30 kilometers (19 miles) south of Durban, the eastern province’s largest city.
“The victims, including a pregnant woman, were gathered at a house shortly before 11pm when armed assailants reportedly entered the premises and opened fire,” Kwa-Zulu Premier Thamsanqa Ntuli said.
“The incident has left the community in profound shock and grief,” he said.
Police said one of the victims died after being taken to hospital.
“Ten victims, including the woman, died at the scene and four were taken ​to hospital, were one of them succumbed to gunshot injuries,” police said.
Some of the victims were known to police, according to the statement. No arrests had yet been made.
Acting police chief Puleng Dimpane said she had launched a 72-hour tracking operation to apprehend the culprits.
Legal and illegal firearms are common in South Africa, as are shootings, which are often fueled by rivalry between criminal gangs or between informal businesses.
South Africa has one of the world’s highest murder rates. Around 60 people are killed each day in the country of around 62 million.
The incident on Tuesday night comes as South Africa is still reeling over a series of femicides near Johannesburg.

item.title: World lagging on key UN biodiversity targets
item.description:
World governments are off track to meet a historic United Nations target to protect at least 30% of the planet’s land and seas by the year 2030, according to a new study published Wednesday.
The research by environmental groups Campaign for Nature and Together for the Ocean shows that about 20% of land and inland waters are designated as protected or conserved, following the signing of the 30×30 goal in 2022.
If nations fully deliver on existing quantified commitments, the estimate could increase to 27% by the turn of the decade, the report said.
The 30x30 goal was adopted under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework at COP15 and was signed by nearly 200 nations that pledged at least $200 billion (about €175 billion) annually to reduce biodiversity loss.
For the world’s oceans, the study says protection is “lagging.”
The coverage is currently at 10% of global ocean and could only reach 12% by 2030, the research revealed.
“The ocean is emerging as one of the defining implementation challenges of 30×30,” Together for the Ocean said, adding that important marine ecosystems, like offshore and deep-sea habitats, remain “vulnerable.”
Last month, the Convention on Biological Diversity, the UN treaty dedicated to the global nature goals, also cautioned that countries were not on track.
The report singled out finance for conservation as “one of the greatest barriers” to reaching global targets.
The research said that between $100 billion and $180 billion was needed each year to make the 2030 target. Current annual spending, however, amounted to just $24 billion.
“The gap is particularly stark for the ocean, where approximately $16 billion is needed annually, but only an estimated $ 1.8 billion is currently spent,” the study said.
From October 19, the UN biodiversity summit in Yerevan will see the nations address the progress shortfall and assess ways of getting back on target.

item.title: Iran airlines cancel flights as US sanctions hit
item.description:
Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tightened sanctions on Iran’s aviation industry in a new effort to cripple its economy.
A travel agent in Tehran told AFP that flights to Baghdad, Muscat, Qatar, Georgia and Azerbaijan had all been suspended, but routes to multiple other destinations remained available, including China.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the new measures on Monday as part of an earlier threat to impose “economic D-Day” on Iran, an attempt to force it into submission following their nearly seven-month war.
But Iran’s aviation sector has already been a target of sanctions for years, and it remains unclear what the full impact will be and whether other countries will comply.
Even after the new sanctions took effect on Wednesday, a flight from Tehran operated by Mahan Air, one of Iran’s biggest carriers, landed in Guangzhou in China, according to tracking data from FlightRadar24.
China on Tuesday said it opposes the US sanctions and called them illegal. A flight to Shanghai was also due to depart on Wednesday, according to Tehran’s international airport.
Some flights to Istanbul were also scheduled, though others had been cancelled, the travel agent in Tehran told AFP.
“The situation is unstable and we are no longer selling tickets for the time being for fear of cancellations,” the agent said, requesting anonymity.
A Mahan flight from Kabul was also expected to arrive in Tehran around midday. According to the website for Tehran’s international airport, other connections to Turkiye and Armenia also remained possible using smaller Iranian airlines, including Varesh.
Flights to Najaf in Iraq and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates were also scheduled.
Bessent on Monday vowed to “shut down” Iranian carriers and punish anyone doing business with them.
“If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” he warned other countries.
The restrictions will further complicate the ability of Iranians to travel abroad or return to their country.
Iranian media also reported cancellations, with the Tasnim news agency on Tuesday citing a civil aviation spokesman as saying that Baghdad and Muscat airports “will no longer accept” Iranian flights.
“Other international flights, including Istanbul, will operate as scheduled and as usual, and at present there are no problems with these flights,” Tasnim said.
According to Tasnim, Iran’s aviation authorities are in talks to reroute Baghdad flights to Najaf, a major destination for Iranian pilgrims.
In Iraq, while the government has not publicly announced plans to enforce the ban, several sources including a senior government official told AFP that Baghdad would comply with the US measures.
The prospect of a suspension of flights between the two countries has sparked concerns from some Iraqi travel agents.
In Najaf, home to one of the most revered Shia Muslim shrines, agent Haidar Shamaa said “most travel companies in the city depend on booking flights” to Iranian airports.
Several travel agencies said panicked clients were calling for updates and were considering switching to land routes, which would mean much longer journeys.

item.title: China’s Xi heads to US for talks with Trump
item.description:
China’s leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he will meet with US President Donald Trump, state media said.
The highly anticipated talks come as the two countries confront rising fears about increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems, and as both sides look to ease tensions on trade.
Xi “left Beijing by special plane,” accompanied by his wife Peng Liyuan, his right-hand man Cai Qi, and foreign minister Wang Yi, among others, state broadcaster CCTV said.
Trump is due to personally meet Xi on his arrival at Joint Base Andrews, before their meetings on Thursday, according to the White House.
The US leader was greeted by China’s vice president when he landed in Beijing for his state visit in May.
Xi and Peng will attend a ceremony at the White House on Thursday morning, which will include a military flyover.
The two leaders are due to hold talks and Trump is set to host Xi for a state dinner at the White House in the evening.
The visit will wrap up on Friday morning where the two presidential couples will have tea at the White House then visit the National Archives to round out the trip.
The White House said that the visit marks “a significant milestone in the relationship between the two countries.”
But the meeting between the two leaders could touch on multiple points of tension, with Trump telling reporters that he will be “discussing almost everything” with Xi.
Trump’s Iran war casts a long shadow, as China seeks to avoid US sanctions against countries dealing with Tehran -- despite reports that Beijing supplied Tehran with intelligence for a strike on US troops.
A trade war is of even greater concern and the world’s two largest economies are still seeking to mitigate the fallout from Trump’s global tariffs.
The threat of war over the island of Taiwan -- which China claims as its territory -- looms large as well.
Analysts, however, have tempered expectations by cautioning there might not be many concrete deals announced.
Preliminary talks between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns, but released little in the way of detail.
Bessant said at the time that the two sides discussed setting up a way to communicate about AI issues called the “US-China AI dialogue.”
“The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries,” Bessent said.
The son of jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai made an appeal to Xi from Washington that his 78-year-old father be released.
Trump said in May, however, that he had discussed Lai’s fate with Xi and his release was unlikely.
But Beijing did release the founder of an underground church, Ezra Jin, after Trump raised his case with Xi.
China’s negotiating arsenal includes its dominance in the supply of rare earths, critical materials used for high-tech products that are vital to US manufacturers.
Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths.
