MLS coach axed for telling female ref 'It's a man's game'
item.description:
Columbus Crew sacked Argentine reserve team coach Federico Higuain for telling a female referee "Don't forget this is a man's game" while refusing to release her from a handshake, the Major League Soccer club said Tuesday.
Higuain, the brother of former Argentina and Real Madrid forward Gonzalo Higuain, had already received a red card and a two-match suspension for the incident before the team dismissed him.
"We determined it's in the best interest of our Club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higua­n from his responsibilities," said Columbus Crew general manager Issa Tall.
"After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our Club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met."
Higuain during follow-up talks with the club was "unwilling to reflect or take accountability for his actions, nor did he offer a public apology," the Athletic reported, citing anonymous club sources.
The incident occurred during a game in MLS's developmental MLS NEXT Pro league.
According to the referees' union, Higuain "committed two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism against a female official -- squeezing her hand and refusing to let go after being told to stop three times.
"This physical intimidation was compounded by a demeaning, sexist remark to the official: 'Don't forget, this is a man's game,'" said the Professional Soccer Referees Association.
The union criticized the league's initial two-game suspension as falling "drastically short," and called for at least a six-game suspension.
"Women make every level of this game better. They should not have to endure intimidation or degrading comments to prove it," it said in a statement.
"Our female officials have proven their excellence on the world stage. They deserve the same respect, dignity, and safe working environment as every other official."

item.title: City Bank, Oxfam to improve climate-resilient Wash facilities in tea garden communities
item.description:
City Bank and Oxfam in Bangladesh have entered into a partnership to improve access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (Wash) services for underserved tea garden communities through climate-resilient solutions.
With a particular focus on the safety, health and dignity of women and girls, the initiative seeks to address critical Wash challenges faced by tea garden communities while strengthening their resilience to the impacts of climate change.
Mashrur Arefin, managing director & CEO of City Bank and Anil Pant, interim country director of Oxfam in Bangladesh signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations at a ceremony held at City Bank Center.
Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman, additional managing director & CFO, Kazi Azizur Rahman, additional managing director & CIO; and Shahriar Jamil Khan, head of brand & marketing of City Bank, along with Mahmuda Sultana, program management adviser, and Halima Akhter Mitu, head of finance, risk and compliance of Oxfam in Bangladesh, and other senior officials from both organizations were present at the signing ceremony.
The partnership brings together City Bank’s broader CSR priorities with Oxfam’s experience in gender justice, climate resilience and community-led development, supporting locally owned and sustainable solutions for tea garden communities.
Mashrur Arefin said: “Access to safe water and sanitation is fundamental to health and dignity. This partnership brings together two of City Bank’s key CSR priorities—women and the environment—to deliver practical, climate-resilient solutions that can make a meaningful difference in the lives of tea garden communities.”
Anil Pant said: “Women tea workers are at the heart of Bangladesh’s tea industry, yet many tea garden communities still face persistent gaps in safe water and sanitation, compounded by growing climate risks. This partnership is about more than infrastructure—it is about dignity, rights and resilience. With City Bank, we aim to support climate-resilient, community-led WASH solutions that improve everyday life and enable communities to sustain change for the long term.”

item.title: JCI Dhaka Sparks launches dengue awareness initiative ‘Fight the Bite: Protect Every Child’
item.description:
JCI Dhaka Sparks has launched its dengue awareness initiative, “Fight the Bite: Protect Every Child,” under the theme “Educate, Protect, Empower,” at Dr Azmal Hospital Ltd, Mirpur.
The initiative was organized in collaboration with OFRON and sponsored by MR Traders, bringing together around 40 participants, including doctors, patients, hospital staff, and other stakeholders.
The program began with a welcome address by local president Raihan Ahmed Dip, who spoke about JCI and JCI Bangladesh and highlighted the importance of community engagement in addressing public health concerns.
The event featured remarks from Dr Hazzaz Bin Mujib, CEO of OFRON, and the ICU Medical Officer of Dr Azmal Hospital, focusing on dengue awareness, prevention, and the importance of taking practical measures to reduce the risk of dengue, particularly among children.
As part of the project's prevention-focused activities, MR Traders donated mosquito nets to children, adding a practical protective measure to the awareness campaign and reinforcing the project's message of prevention alongside education.
Mir Sadman Ali, director of Dr Azmal Hospital, was present at the program along with distinguished doctors, medical professionals, and hospital officials.
The program was coordinated by Dr Fatematuzzannat Brishty, specialist in public health administration, and Mostafijur Rahman, PR and media committee chairperson of JCI Dhaka Sparks.
Through “Fight the Bite: Protect Every Child,” JCI Dhaka Sparks aims to promote greater awareness of dengue prevention and encourage communities to take proactive measures to protect children and vulnerable members of society.

item.title: PPRC: Economic empowerment next step for financial inclusion
item.description:
Bangladesh’s next phase of financial inclusion must move beyond expanding access to financial services and focus on whether people and enterprises can use finance to invest, expand businesses, create employment and strengthen economic resilience, speakers said at a national policy dialogue organized by the Power and Participation Research Centre (PPRC).
The PPRC Real Economy Dialogue on “Financial Inclusion 2.0: Policy Goals, Transactions Ecology and Sustainable Roadmap” was held on September 19 at Hotel InterContinental Dhaka.
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, MP attended as chief guest, while PPRC executive chairman Hossain Zillur Rahman chaired and moderated the dialogue.
Presenting PPRC’s Financial Inclusion 2.0 framework, Rahman said Bangladesh had made significant gains through microfinance, mobile financial services and agent banking, but the nature of the challenge had changed.
“Inclusion has not necessarily led to empowerment in every case,” he said.
PPRC identified access to appropriate finance for cottage, micro, small and medium enterprises as a major next challenge. Collateral-based lending, complex procedures and unsuitable financing continue to keep many entrepreneurs outside formal credit.
Dr. Fazlul Kader, Executive Director of PKSF, called for “prosperity financing that enables capital formation,” adding: “The ultimate indicator is employment.”
Sabbir Ahmed, Visa’s country manager for Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, said: “Our traditional SME lending system is not fit for purpose.”
On the disconnect between transactions and lending, he added: “Our payment infrastructure and credit infrastructure do not talk to each other. They have to talk.”
Mohammad Mamdudur Rashid, managing director and CEO of UCB, said: “Only when credit scoring becomes a low-cost commodity can credit reach the truly marginal level.”
Mohammad Helal Uddin, executive vice-chairman of the Microcredit Regulatory Authority, stressed the need to connect borrowers’ banking and microfinance histories: “If the bank CIB is not joined with the MFI CIB, any score is incomplete.”
On the transition towards a digital financial future, Kamal Quadir, CEO of bKash, said: “For a digital future transition, we must have ecological preparation.”
Md Arfan Ali, founder and chairman of Zaytoon Business Solutions and former managing director of Bank Asia, said: “When you speak of Inclusion 2.0, interoperability must be priority number one.”
The dialogue also focused on how digital reform can proceed without weakening the agent networks and commercial incentives on which the existing financial system depends.
On Bangla QR and Zero IRF, Kaiser A Chowdhury, chairman of Nagad, asked: “Can our banks fill the vacuum of some 1.5 million agents overnight?”
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, managing director and CEO of Mutual Trust Bank, said: “Every stakeholder needs to see an incentive, otherwise cash becomes easier and cheaper.”
On barriers to wider smartphone and data adoption, Mahtab Uddin Ahmed, former president of ICMAB and former CEO of Robi Axiata, said: “Bangladesh is the only country in the world where voice price has a mandatory floor price … so there is disincentive in the data business.”
Calling for greater coherence between policy objectives and implementation, Muhammad Abdul Mazid, former chairman of NBR and chairman of the Social Development Foundation, said: “The government must come out of self-contradiction.”
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury identified robust internet connectivity as fundamental economic infrastructure.
“Everyone says power, gas. I would add one more: robust internet,” he said. “Without robust internet, the digital economy has no future.”
The minister said the Cabinet-approved “one citizen, one wallet” initiative was under process, supported wider credit-rating coverage and nano-lending, and said digital banking would move forward soon.
He also stressed the importance of safeguards: “You cannot do digitalization, AI operation, without guardrails.”
The dialogue additionally covered agricultural and retail finance, microfinance regulation, digital fraud and cybersecurity, smartphone affordability, financial literacy and the integration of credit information.
Closing the session, Hossain Zillur Rahman said Financial Inclusion 2.0 must connect financial empowerment, enterprise growth, employment and an integrated digital financial system, while preserving the strengths of the ecosystem Bangladesh has already built.
“A big-bang approach is not the relevant way forward,” he said. “It is about getting those second- and third-order policy steps right.”
PPRC will draw on the dialogue to develop a comprehensive Financial Inclusion 2.0 policy paper, setting out the proposed policy framework, areas of convergence and issues requiring further policy work.

item.title: Ex-Khulna University student confesses to beating Ajmul in court
item.description:
A former Khulna University student has confessed in court to his involvement in the beating of North Western University student Md Ajmul Hossain, saying two other people also took part in the assault, according to police.
Hasnat Habib Rifat, a cash officer at Krishi Bank who was arrested in Pirojpur in connection with the case, made the statement before a Khulna court on Tuesday night.
Investigating Officer Sub-Inspector Nazmul Haque said Rifat gave a statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before Judge Ibrahim Khalil of Khulna Metropolitan Magistrate Court-4. He was later sent to jail.
According to police, Rifat said former Khulna University students Pratap Sarkar and Tarek Hasan Rubel, owner of a juice shop near Khanjahan Ali Hall, also took part in beating Ajmul.
Police said Rifat and Pratap lived in the same mess as Ajmul, while Rubel went there after learning about the incident and joined the assault.
Harintana police station Officer-in-Charge Iqbal Hossain said eight people, including Rifat, Pratap and Rubel, were present during the assault.
“Interrogation is yielding further important information,” he said.
According to the OC, Rifat told police that Ajmul fell from the roof at one point during the beating.
Iqbal also confirmed that Rifat works as a cash officer at Krishi Bank’s Nawapara branch in Bagerhat.
He said none of the three arrested suspects was named in the initial First Information Report, although police believe they were directly involved in the incident.
Police are continuing operations to arrest the other suspects. Pratap and Rubel, who are currently in police custody, may be produced before a court on Wednesday afternoon.
Rifat, a student of the 16th batch of Khulna University’s Fisheries and Marine Resource Technology Department, was detained by SRB-6 from Kuriana Adabari village under Nesarabad police station in Pirojpur late Monday night.
Rubel was picked up from near Khanjahan Ali Hall on Tuesday afternoon.
On Wednesday afternoon, a joint team of the Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) and Harintana police detained Pratap in Wazirpur, Barishal.
Lt Col Nistar Ahmed, commander of SRB-6, said the battalion launched a parallel investigation following the murder and later assisted police in apprehending the suspects.
Rifat and Rubel were subsequently handed over to Harintana police, he said.
Ahaduzzaman Mia, deputy commissioner of the Metropolitan DB, said information technology was used to trace Pratap’s location in Wazirpur.
He said Pratap was detained around 5pm and later handed over to Harintana police.
According to police, Ajmul was taken to the fourth floor and rooftop of the mess late on September 18 and beaten after being accused of theft.
At one point, he fell from the roof of the four-storey building. He was later taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
Police are investigating whether Ajmul jumped from the roof or was pushed or thrown after being beaten.
Ajmul’s father, Kutub Uddin, filed a murder case with Harintana police station, naming four people and accusing 20-25 unidentified individuals.

Maksuda denies argument with Mariyam as DB questions her, Nazrul
item.description:
Maksuda Islam, first wife of Jamaat-e-Islami MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, told investigators she had no argument with his second wife, Mariyam Khatun, before Mariyam’s death.
Maksuda and Gazi Nazrul, who were arrested in a case filed over abetting Mariyam’s suicide, were questioned face-to-face by the Tejgaon division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) on Tuesday.
An investigation officer said important information relevant to the case was obtained during the questioning.
After Maksuda’s one-day remand ended on Tuesday, investigation officer Inspector Mohammad Salahuddin produced her before the court and sought an order to keep her in jail.
In his petition, he said important information related to the case had been obtained by questioning Maksuda on remand and that it would assist the investigation.
Meanwhile, Gazi Nazrul was being questioned on a four-day remand, with Tuesday being the first day.
According to a source close to the investigation, DB officials questioned Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda together.
It was initially reported that Gazi Nazrul had gone to court on the day of the incident in connection with a case and found Maryiam’s body after returning home. However, the investigation source said both Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda admitted during questioning that they were at home when the incident occurred.
Gazi Nazrul told investigators that he left home in the morning and returned around 2pm. Some leaders and activists from his constituency had come to the house around noon, and he had lunch with them after speaking to them.
After lunch, he went to Mariyam’s room to see whether she had eaten but found the door locked from inside. After knocking and calling out without receiving any response, he eventually informed the police.
Police later arrived, broke open the door and found Mariyam’s body hanging from the ceiling fan.
On Sunday evening, police recovered the hanging body of 19-year-old Mariyam from a flat in Building 5 of NAM Bhaban, opposite the Parliament complex.
The flat belongs to Gazi Nazrul, who lived there with his first wife Maksuda and second wife Mariyam.
That night, Mariyam’s father, Masum Billah, filed a case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station accusing Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda and Mariyam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman of abetting her suicide.
The two accused were shown arrested and produced before a court on Monday. Following a hearing on a seven-day remand plea, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Ehsanul Islam granted Gazi Nazrul four days’ remand and Maksuda one day’s remand.

item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman began his day on Tuesday by attending a breakfast reception hosted by United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres for world leaders and their spouses at the UN headquarters in New York.
The breakfast was held at the North Dialogue Lounge at 8:00am local time, said Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
Tarique Rahman and his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman attended the reception, where the UN secretary-general exchanged greetings with them, he said.
The prime minister arrived in New York on Monday evening to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA).
After breakfast, Tarique Rahman is scheduled to attend the opening session of the UNGA and hold a series of meetings with heads of government and state on the sidelines of the session.
He is scheduled to deliver his speech at the General Debate of the 81st UN General Assembly on Thursday afternoon.

item.title: Minister: Fuel price hike unlikely to push up commodity prices much
item.description:
Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said Tuesday the recent increase in fuel prices is unlikely to have a significant impact on the prices of essential commodities.
He made the comments while responding to questions from journalists after distributing raincoats among tea workers at the factory ground of Lakkatura Tea Garden in Sylhet.
The minister said strict monitoring would be carried out to prevent unscrupulous traders from taking advantage of the situation.
Muktadir said the opposition is an elected opposition party and should behave responsibly instead of making sensational statements.
Earlier, raincoats were distributed among 1,980 tea workers from different tea gardens.
Addressing the tea workers, the minister said the government is taking various steps to increase the income of tea gardens.
“Just a few days ago, we held a meeting on the prime minister’s instructions to make tea gardens profitable,” he said.
He said discussions are underway on whether timber, spice and other trees could be planted in tea gardens without harming tea plants.
Solar power facilities will also be installed in gardens where feasible, he added.
“The main objective is to increase the income of the gardens. If we can increase their income, we will also be able to increase the wages of the workers properly,” the minister said.
Highlighting various initiatives to improve the living standards of tea workers, Muktadir said ambulances are being arranged for tea garden workers.
Schools will be established in gardens where there are none, while roads inside the gardens will also be repaired, he said.
The event was organised by the Sylhet Sadar Upazila administration.
Sylhet City Corporation Administrator Abdul Quiyum Choudhury, Deputy Commissioner Abdullah Al Mamun, District Council Administrator Abul Kaher Chowdhury, Mahanagar BNP President Nasim Hossain, among others, attended the program.

item.title: 7-year-old boy’s body stuffed in sack found in Bhola
item.description:
Police on Tuesday recovered the body of a seven-year-old boy stuffed in a sack two days after he went missing in Borhanuddin upazila of Bhola.
The body of Md Ismail, son of Md Akbar Hossain, was recovered in the morning from a canal near Muslimpara in Ward No-5 of the municipality, said Ashrafuddin, officer-in-charge (OC) of Borhanuddin police station.
Police detained a 22-year-old youth, Md Rokon, for questioning in connection.
According to the family, Ismail left home to play at around 10:30am on Sunday.
When he did not return home by the afternoon, family members and locals began searching for him.
As he could not be found despite extensive searches his father filed a General Diary (GD) with the police station.
Locals spotted a sack floating in a canal near Muslimpara and informed police. Police went to the spot and recovered the boy’s body from inside the sack.
Relatives later identified the body as Ismail’s.
The victim’s family alleged Ismail’s father, Akbar Hossain, and Rokon were locked in an altercation over the purchase of a mobile phone.
Relatives claimed that Rokon threatened Akbar at the time.
OC Ashrafuddin said the boy’s body was sent to the morgue at Bhola Sadar Hospital for an autopsy.
The cause of death and the circumstances surrounding the boy’s death have not yet been confirmed, he said.

item.title: Measles: Death toll 1,065 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
The death toll from suspected and confirmed measles cases in Bangladesh has reached 1,065, with two more suspected measles-related deaths reported in the 24 hours to till 8am Tuesday.
The latest deaths were reported in Dhaka and Khulna, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the two deaths reported in the latest 24-hour period, none was confirmed as a measles-related death.
Since March 15, a total of 964 suspected measles-related deaths have been reported, while 101 deaths have been confirmed as measles-related.
Meanwhile, 1,257 new suspected measles cases were reported in the 24 hours to 8am Tuesday, including 92 confirmed cases.
The cumulative number of suspected measles cases has reached 182,292 since March 15, while 20,738 cases have been confirmed.
During the period, 160,980 suspected measles patients were admitted to hospitals and 154,510 were discharged.
The figures were provided in the DGHS health bulletin on Tuesday, based on data from the Health Emergency Operations Centre and Control Room.

item.title: Foreign Secretary Siam to move to Delhi as new Bangladesh envoy
item.description:
Asad Alam Siam, the current foreign secretary of Bangladesh, will soon move to New Delhi as the new Bangladesh High Commissioner to India.
A copy of the “agrément” (an official approval by the host country) has already been handed over to Bangladesh, a senior official told UNB on Tuesday.
The foreign secretary is now in New York accompanying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as a member of the Bangladesh delegation.
The government is scheduled to appoint Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury, the immediate past permanent representative of Bangladesh to the United Nations in New York, as the next foreign secretary.
Foreign Secretary Siam will take up his responsibilities soon as Bangladesh's High Commissioner to India, a posting widely seen as one of the country's most important diplomatic assignments, officials said.
Bangladesh's current High Commissioner to India, M Riaz Hamidullah, will take up his new assignment as Permanent Representative of Bangladesh to the United Nations in Geneva next month.
Siam has completed one year in office, having assumed the post on June 20, 2025.
A career diplomat, Ambassador Siam joined the Bangladesh Foreign Service in 1995.
Throughout his distinguished diplomatic career, he has served extensively both at home and abroad.
Prior to his current appointment, he served as Bangladesh's ambassador to the United States, with concurrent accreditation to Guyana, and as Bangladesh's Permanent Representative to the World Bank (WB) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
From 2023 to 2024, Ambassador Siam served as Bangladesh's Ambassador to Austria, with concurrent accreditation to Hungary and Slovenia, and as Permanent Representative to the United Nations Office in Vienna and the OPEC Fund.
Before serving in Austria, Ambassador Siam was Bangladesh's Ambassador to the Philippines from 2017 to 2021, with concurrent accreditation to Palau, and as Bangladesh's Permanent Representative to the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI).
Earlier in his career, he served as the first Consul General at the Bangladesh Consulate General in Milan, Italy; as Assistant High Commissioner at the Bangladesh Assistant High Commission in Manchester, UK; and as a junior diplomat at the Bangladesh Embassies in Jakarta and Bangkok.
In addition to his overseas assignments, he held several important positions at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka.
He served as inspector general of missions (IGM) at the ministry and as Rector of the Foreign Service Academy.
He also served as chief of protocol and director general of the Europe and EU Wing. As Director, he served in the offices of the Foreign Adviser and the Foreign Secretary.
Ambassador Noman Chowdhury joined the Bangladesh Foreign Service in 1998.
Prior to his current posting, he served as Bangladesh's Ambassador to Nepal from November 2020 to December 2024.
During his diplomatic career spanning more than two decades, he has served in various capacities at Bangladesh missions abroad, including the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, the Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations in New York, the Consulate General of Bangladesh in New York, and the Bangladesh High Commission in Islamabad.
At the headquarters, he served in the United Nations, Economic Affairs, Administration, Protocol, External Publicity and Southeast Asia Wings, as well as at the Foreign Service Academy.

item.title: France says it does not ask Bangladesh to choose sides
item.description:
France Ambassador to Bangladesh Jean-Marc Séré-Charlet on Tuesday said France does not want Bangladesh to choose between Europe and other partners, stressing that they are ready to strengthen their engagement with Bangladesh.
“So, France, Europe, we never say to Bangladesh - you choose between us and them. That's what I said. I mentioned at the very beginning. We build partnership. Partnership is not excluding. It is involving,” he told diplomatic correspondents at the “DCAB Talk” noting that the Franco-Bangladeshi relations have great potential.
Diplomatic Correspondents Association, Bangladesh (DCAB) hosted its flagship event at the Jatiya Press Club. DCAB President AKM Moinuddin and its General Secretary Emrul Kayesh also spoke.
On Bangladesh’s plan to purchase Airbus aircraft, the French ambassador said Biman Bangladesh Airlines chose Airbus for technical and business reasons rather than political considerations.
“That's why, for very good reasons and technical reasons, Biman has chosen Airbus,” he said, adding that discussions over the proposed aircraft deal are continuing and that such negotiations can take time.
“Biman maintained its interest with Airbus and discussions are still going on. We know it may take sometimes, because we want discussions to be done in the best manner possible,” the Ambassador said, noting that he could not disclose details of the technical negotiations because the deal is between Biman and Airbus.
“So it may take time, but I can assure you that negotiations have been going on and very well with others. It's an Airbus contract, which will come, in due time, with Airbus signing with Biman. So I'm not worried at all,” said the French envoy, expressing confidence in both the government and Biman regarding the negotiations.
The envoy said this is a good test for the present government. “So for me, it's not an issue. Wait some time, some days, and we'll see what happens, but things are going well.”
He also talked about Bangladesh’s engagement with Europe, including the possibility of a free trade agreement (FTA) and cooperation in the aviation sector.
The ambassador stressed that France and Europe are not seeking to exclude other countries from Bangladesh. “So we are not in an exclusion mode.”
He said the European Union has signed FTAs with several countries but Bangladesh has yet to be included in that group.
“We have signed FTAs with many countries. Vietnam, India, Australia, Canada, not Bangladesh. You are not on the map,” he said.
“So if you want to be more on the map, if you want Europe to engage, you have to show the interest of engaging in the long term partnership. That's why Airbus matters,” the envoy added.
He pointed to Bangladesh’s strong trade relationship with Europe, particularly in the readymade garment sector.
The ambassador said France and Europe remain open to partnership, while cautioning that opportunities could be missed if Bangladesh decides not to move in that direction. “We believe in partnership. We want to create a true partnership, a long-standing partnership.”
He also highlighted cooperation between Bangladesh and French companies in high-technology sectors.
Ambassador Séré-Charlet said France is a “long-standing, reliable, predictable, and benevolent” partner for Bangladesh.
And like Bangladesh, he said, it seeks to promote - cooperation rather than confrontation; multilateralism; peace in the world.
The envoy said France is a secular country that does not discriminate against its citizens based on their beliefs, respects all religions and notably Islam, maintains strong and longstanding ties with the Arab and Muslim world, and supports the Palestinian people.
He said France shares many values and interests with Bangladesh, also as the only member state of the European Union that is a major power in the Indo-Pacific region, which is home to 2 million of its citizens.
The envoy said France's diplomatic and strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region, particularly in its relationship with Bangladesh, are centered around promoting a multilateral "third way."
He said that, faced with the growing rivalry between the United States and China, France is positioning itself as a balancing power, leveraging its status as an Indian Ocean nation. “Promoting a "third way" in the face of hegemonic powers means - strategic autonomy, maritime security and stability in the Indian Ocean.”
“We need the countries that share the same values and goals (peaceful international relations) be more assertive and more proactive, to cooperate more, and to demonstrate, through their example, the effectiveness of this model,” said the French envoy.
He said they are seeing an unprecedented rapprochement with Canada, as well as with other countries. “It is not only geopolitical but also economy and business. I believe that Franco-Bangladeshi relations have great potential.”

item.title: Bumper jute harvest, fair prices bring smiles to Sariakandi farmers
item.description:
Farmers in Sariakandi upazila of Bogra have produced and sold jute worth nearly Tk 134 crore this season, benefiting from favourable weather, a sharp increase in cultivation and better market prices.
According to the Sariakandi Upazila Agriculture Office, jute was cultivated on 5,055 hectares this year against a target of 3,105 hectares. Production reached 14,098 tonnes.
Based on the minimum market price of Tk 3,800 per maund, the total value of this year's production is estimated at Tk 133.93 crore, the agriculture office said.
Sariakandi has long been a major jute-growing area. The upazila's sandy loam soil, formed by the Jamuna and Bangali river systems, is considered highly suitable for jute cultivation.
Farmers had reduced jute cultivation in recent years due to falling prices and rising labour costs. However, improved prices last year encouraged them to expand cultivation this season.
Jute is currently being sold at between Tk 3,800 and Tk 4,300 per maund. Farmers are also earning additional income by selling jute sticks after keeping a portion for household fuel.
Abu Sayeed, a jute farmer from Kuripara village in Kajla Union, said he doubled the area under jute cultivation this year after making a profit last season.
“Last year, I sold jute for up to Tk 3,500 per maund. This year, I harvested an average of 11 maunds per bigha and sold the jute for Tk 4,100 per maund,” he said.
He said selling the surplus jute sticks after keeping enough for household use had provided him with additional income.
Sunil Kumar Pramanik, a jute trader in Sariakandi municipality, said traders bought jute for up to Tk 3,600 per maund during last year's harvesting season.
“Outside the harvesting season, the price rose to as high as Tk 5,500 per maund. This year, we have purchased jute at between Tk 3,600 and Tk 4,300 per maund,” he said.
Mohammad Ali Jinnah, agriculture officer of Sariakandi Upazila, said favourable weather had contributed to the bumper yield.
“The soil in Sariakandi is highly suitable for jute cultivation. With support from the agriculture office, farmers cultivated jute on a much larger area this year, and the yield was also good,” he said.
He said farmers were making good profits as jute prices had remained higher than in previous years.
“We hope jute cultivation will increase further in the coming years,” he added.

item.title: Floodwaters damage vegetables in Rajshahi char areas
item.description:
Floodwaters from the Padma River have damaged vegetable crops across char areas of Paba upazila in Rajshahi, leaving farmers worried about recovering their investments.
Just a few days ago, the charlands in Alimganj and Kasba of Haripur Union were lush with pointed gourd, cucumber, bitter gourd, bottle gourd, cauliflower, cabbage and tomato fields.
But rising water from the Padma has submerged several plots. In some areas, water has reached waist level, while in others, crops have rotted after remaining underwater for days.
Some farmers are trying to drain water from their fields in a last-ditch effort to save the remaining crops, while others are uprooting plants that have already decayed.
During a recent visit to the affected areas, several vegetable fields were found submerged. Early varieties of cauliflower, cabbage and tomato plants had rotted, while pointed gourd, bitter gourd, bottle gourd and cucumber plants were also badly damaged.
Farmer Akbar Ali of Kasba was seen pulling out rotted pointed gourd plants from one of his plots.
He said floodwaters had damaged one bigha of pointed gourd, 10 katha of cucumber and five katha of ridge gourd.
“The pointed gourd plants have rotted and have to be pulled out,” he said.
“Even the pointed gourd plants that are still okay are now dying. If that's the case, then everything is finished.”
Farmers said water remained stagnant for around seven days in several plots in the Kasba char area, causing extensive damage to crops.
Farmer Md Nazrul Islam said nearly 10 katha of bitter gourd, 10 katha of cucumber, 10 katha of bottle gourd, 1.5 bighas of different varieties of cabbage, 15 katha of pointed gourd and five katha of tomatoes were damaged.
According to Nazrul, he had invested around Tk10,000 in tomatoes, Tk30,000 in pointed gourd, Tk10,000 in bitter gourd, Tk20,000 in cucumber, Tk15,000 in bottle gourd and Tk30,000-Tk35,000 in cabbage.
The losses have placed a heavy financial burden on him, he said.
Another farmer, Shahriar Rahman Russell, lost nearly 10,000 cauliflower and cabbage seedlings. Had the crops survived, he expected to sell them for Tk300,000-Tk350,000.
“We are farmers. We don't want any crops to be destroyed. We tried our best to save them. But it still wasn't possible,” Russell said.
Shamim Al Mamun, another pointed gourd farmer, said he had lost 15 katha of pointed gourd to the floodwaters, causing losses of at least Tk200,000.
He said the losses were particularly significant because this is the peak harvesting season for pointed gourd.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), the sudden flooding has affected crops on a total of 309.59 hectares of land in Paba, Bagha and Godagari upazilas of Rajshahi.
Of the affected land, 45.24 hectares are vegetables, 85.39 hectares black gram, 11.46 hectares transplanted Aman, 25 hectares transplanted Aus, 102 hectares turmeric, 25 hectares papaya, 10 hectares guava and 5.50 hectares summer onion seedbeds.
In Paba, 7.24 hectares of vegetables, 6.39 hectares of black gram and 0.46 hectares of transplanted Aman have been affected.
In Godagari, 10 hectares of vegetables, 17 hectares of black gram and 25 hectares of transplanted Aus were damaged.
Bagha has recorded the largest affected area, with 28 hectares of vegetables, 62 hectares of black gram, 11 hectares of transplanted Aman, 102 hectares of turmeric, 25 hectares of papaya, 10 hectares of guava and 5.50 hectares of summer onion seedbeds affected.
Zahurul Haque, sub-assistant agriculture officer of the Alimganj Block in Paba, visited the damaged fields in Kasba.
He said the char areas were inundated as water levels in the Padma rose due to upstream flows.
“As a result, various vegetables were partially damaged,” he said.
He added that farmers had managed to save around 60% of the crops by raising embankments and draining water from the fields.
A list of affected farmers is currently being prepared, he said, adding that farmers are also being advised on how to care for the damaged crops and save those that remain viable.
Mostafa Kamal Hossain, deputy director of the Rajshahi Department of Agricultural Extension, said crops had been damaged by flooding in areas along the Padma.
He said the administration would assist affected farmers and that an assessment of the damage was currently underway.

item.title: Experts urge worker-focused energy transition in apparel sector
item.description:
Experts and industry stakeholders have called for a worker-centred just energy transition in Bangladesh’s apparel sector, stressing that the shift towards renewable energy, automation and green production must be accompanied by workers’ rights, workplace safety, reskilling and social protection.
They said the apparel industry needs to invest in clean energy, reduce energy waste and adopt future-ready technologies to remain competitive in a rapidly changing global economy, while ensuring that technological and energy transitions do not leave workers without jobs or adequate support.
The speakers made the remarks at a dialogue titled “Improving Policy Arrangements for Just Energy Transition (JET) in Bangladesh’s Apparel Sector from a Labour Perspective” at 90’s Lounge in Gazipur on Tuesday.
The event was jointly organized by the National Alliance for Just Transition Bangladesh (NAJTB), Bangladesh Labour Foundation (BLF), Bangladesh Institute of Labour Studies (BILS) and Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF), with support from Oxfam in Bangladesh.
The program was part of MJF’s Fashion Forward project, which focuses on making the transition in the apparel sector fair, inclusive and responsive to workers’ rights, livelihoods and workplace realities.
Amer Salim, chairman of the BGMEA Standing Committee on Just Transition, said Bangladesh’s garment sector, which employs nearly 40 lakh workers and contributes 10.4% to GDP, must prepare for rapid changes in the global labour market.
He stressed the need to upskill and reskill workers for future-ready jobs, promote digital learning, uphold the dignity of labour and adopt intelligent factory engineering to build a sustainable and competitive apparel industry.
Experts and industry stakeholders attend a dialogue on a worker-centred just energy transition in Bangladesh’s apparel sector at 90’s Lounge in Gazipur on Tuesday, September 22, 2026. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Md Anowar Hossen, chief coordinator of NAJTB, said a fair and sustainable industrial transition requires technical reskilling, workplace safety and environmental accountability.
He said modern training, reduced operational carelessness and green standards across industrial hubs are essential to ensuring economic growth protects workers’ dignity, safety and well-being.
Asaduzzaman, assistant inspector general (Health) of the Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE), urged industries to reduce their reliance on non-renewable energy.
“Industries must move away from excessive dependence on non-renewable fuels,” he said.
He also called on factory owners to install rooftop solar systems, reduce energy wastage and promote a culture of energy conservation.
Tania Tabassum, additional deputy commissioner of Gazipur, said workers should not bear the cost of technological changes in factories.
“Automation and technological change must not treat workers as disposable,” she said.
She urged factory owners and industry associations to provide structured training when new technologies are introduced, and called for government incentives, lower import tariffs on renewable energy infrastructure and green financing to support the transition.
Trade union leader Noimul Ahsan Juwel called for a dedicated RMG Just Transition Fund, financed by factory owners, buyers and international partners.
He said workers displaced by automation should receive at least a three-month stipend and targeted reskilling support, while urging the formalisation of Bangladesh’s large informal workforce to ensure job security, workplace safety and social protection.
Pablo Neruda, deputy program manager of MJF, said automation must not undermine workers’ rights and livelihoods.
“Automation must not take away workers’ fundamental rights and livelihoods,” he said, urging factory owners to reskill workers affected by automation.
“Through the Fashion Forward initiative, MJF is committed to taking workers’ grassroots realities from Gazipur to the national policy level,” he added.

item.title: UK king braces as memoir by Diana’s brother goes on sale
item.description:
Charles Spencer’s book about his late sister, Princess Diana, packed with explosive revelations is published Tuesday, after searing extracts prompted a rare and sharp rebuttal from King Charles III.
Almost three decades after Diana was killed in a car crash in Paris in 1997, people remain fascinated by her life and tragic death.
“Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” a memoir written by Diana’s younger brother, has been published by Penguin and translated into 12 languages.
But extracts serialized in the British tabloid the Daily Mail over the past few days have triggered sensational headlines.
Spencer has said he wrote the book to “speak on Diana’s behalf” and correct “untruths that have become accepted over time.”
“Diana would be cheering from the rafters at this book, I have no doubt about that,” he told the Mail on Sunday at the weekend.
Published excerpts claimed her ex-husband Charles, then Prince of Wales, and now the king, told Spencer in a phone call shortly after Diana’s death: “Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.”
Her death, aged just 36, sparked an outpouring of grief in Britain for the woman dubbed “the people’s princess.”
And it triggered accusations that the then monarch, Queen Elizabeth II, failed to respond swiftly with empathy and understanding.
Spencer claimed Charles had “sounded giddily elated, like a lottery winner” at the news of Diana’s demise.
And he said Charles “went ballistic” after he insisted Diana would not have wanted her sons, princes William and Harry, then aged 15 and 12, to walk behind her coffin in her funeral procession.
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson issued a rare reaction from the 77-year-old king, saying: “His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss.”
“The king is plainly furious, Buckingham Palace almost never issues any statement like that,” BBC journalist Laura Kuenssberg said during a Friday interview.
“Those are exactly the words he said,” Spencer assured her, adding: “I don’t hear (King Charles) saying he didn’t say that.”
Spencer criticized the palace’s implication that his grief had affected his recollection, telling The Mail on Sunday: “It is not every day you wake up to find you’ve been gaslit by the king.”
He also dubbed it a “rather poor imitation” of the palace’s response to Prince Harry and his wife Meghan’s claims of royal racism five years ago -- which was that “recollections may vary.”
Charles and Diana’s tumultuous marriage between 1981 and 1996 was regularly featured in British newspapers.
And Spencer reveals Diana had at times contemplated suicide, driving down to Beachy Head, a notorious clifftop in southern England where people used to deliberately fall to their deaths.
But her love for her sons “stopped her from going further,” he writes.
Spencer also recalled Diana told him she and Charles were divorcing because he was “in love with his valet,” adding he did not ask why “she would believe such an improbable thing.”
Charles later married his long-time mistress, Camilla Parker Bowles, who is now the queen.
But royal experts have questioned some of the book’s claims.
Royal biographer Robert Hardman wrote on X that he witnessed Charles, rather than elated, “distraught and in tears” at Diana’s funeral.
Andrew Morton, author of the 1992 book “Diana: Her True Story,” in a comment in The Times wrote that Spencer’s claims about the phone call with Charles were “incendiary and disputed.”
While royal commentator Jennie Bond told the BBC the memoir was a “vindictive account.”
Spencer, 62, has worked as a US television journalist and calls himself an historian.
He inherited the Spencer family’s stately home Althorp, where he and Diana grew up. She is buried on an island in the grounds.
After her death, he accused the media of having “blood on their hands” and in his raw eulogy at Diana’s funeral, he vowed to always look out for her two sons.
But he did not mention her beau Dodi Fayed, who was also killed in the Paris crash, even though in the memoir he praised the son of Harrods owner, Mohamed Al-Fayed, for being “kind to Diana.”
But in a shocking claim, Spencer wrote Diana had felt “revulsion” for Mohamed Al-Fayed who had squeezed her buttocks and said “in a leery, suggestive tone, ‘and in Egypt, father-in-law gets first go.’”
Spencer also told the BBC the media’s “cancerous influence” on Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, recalled Diana’s hounding by the British press.

item.title: Macron says talks with Trump on Red Sea, Ukraine ‘constructive’
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday he had “very constructive” talks with his US counterpart Donald Trump on the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine.
Macron spoke with Trump after arriving in New York ahead of the annual gathering of world leaders at the United Nations.
“We had a very good discussion. It was very constructive,” he told reporters after the meeting.
Macron said there was a “willingness to reopen (the Strait of) Hormuz,” a vital shipping route for the world’s oil and gas, which has been blockaded by Iran during the war in the Middle East.
“Several solutions were discussed... which would make it possible, without a comprehensive deal, to find ways and means of allowing more container ships and tankers to go through,” Macron said without giving additional details.
“The other issue we talked about was the situation in the Red Sea... It’s important for global prices,” he said.
The Red Sea has become a key oil shipping route with the Strait of Hormuz blocked, but the takeover of a key strait by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis has complicated shipping operations there.
On Russia and Ukraine, Macron said he pressed Trump on the issue of supplying defensive weapons systems to Kyiv.
Macron and Trump discussed “the need to help our Ukrainian friends faster and more strongly in terms of (missile) interceptors, because that is... a defensive measure,” the French leader said.
Macron said in a post on X that they also discussed “the prospect of an energy truce and a moratorium in the Black Sea.”
He told reporters he would also discuss the topic with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
“It is clear that today we need to help Ukraine’s energy system,” he said.
Macron met Zelensky on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Monday.
Going into the high-stakes meeting with Trump, a French official briefed that Macron was prepared to face the US president with “total candor.”
The French president said Trump was “very amenable and we were able to go into detail on these two conflicts, which are obviously important for peace in the world and for our security.”
Macron traveled to New York from Saint Pierre and Miquelon, a small French territory off Canada’s Atlantic coast, where he met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Carney has been embroiled in a war of words with Trump over a failed effort between the United States and Canada to strike a trade deal, resulting in tit-for-tat tariffs.

item.title: Respiratory problems climb past 170,000 cases in haze-hit Indonesia
item.description:
More than 170,000 respiratory cases were recorded in regions affected by haze in Indonesia, a health ministry official said Tuesday, as the country battles for weeks to control fires that caused the toxic smog.
Blazes in Borneo, Sumatra and Papua have blanketed parts of the vast archipelago of more than 280 million people, as well as neighboring Malaysia and Singapore, sending air quality indices plummeting.
The toxic smog contains pollutants including PM 2.5, a fine particulate matter smaller than a human hair that could carry health risk such as respiratory infections, health ministry official Then Suyanti told a news conference.
“There were 174,694 cases of acute respiratory infections between August and September 21 in areas affected by forest and land fires,” she said.
More than 40,000 of the recorded respiratory cases affected toddlers, she said.
The overall figure, reported in seven haze-affected provinces across Indonesia, was up from over 113,000 cases reported as of September 9.
The health ministry had mobilized aid including oxygen concentrators, face masks and oxygen canisters to the affected regions, Then said.
“We advise (the public) to reduce outdoor activities when air quality worsen, use mask and maintain hydration,” she said.
Indonesia regularly battles wildfires during the dry season, which typically runs from July to October.
But the blazes are more intense this year, coinciding with what is expected to be the strongest El Nino climate phenomenon since comparable records began four decades ago.
Experts also blame climate change, decades of forest degradation and slash-and-burn land-clearing practises that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape.

item.title: DSE: Investors’ Protector Fund to refund investors up to Tk5 lakh
item.description:
The Investors’ Protection Fund (IPF) has decided to fully reimburse investment amounts of up to Tk5 lakh to affected investors of five defaulting brokerage houses in the capital market. This disbursement process will begin on September 28.
As a result, approximately 17,332 investors across these five brokerage houses—representing nearly 97% of all affected investors—will receive a full refund of their invested capital.
Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) Chairman Mominul Islam announced these details at a press conference organized by the DSE on Tuesday (September 22).
He stated that 17,925 investors are currently affected across the five defaulting brokerage houses. So far, approximately Tk37.60 crore in compensation has been disbursed through these houses and the Investors’ Protection Fund.
The DSE chairman mentioned that legal action would be taken against the defaulting brokerage houses to recover the remaining investors' funds.
If necessary, initiatives will be taken to recover funds by selling the shares of these institutions, liquidating their holdings in the DSE, and selling the personal assets of their directors.
Furthermore, if required, arrangements will be made to settle the claims of those 593 investors using future contributions to the IPF.
During the press conference, the chairman noted that for over two years, there have been no high-quality IPOs or new listings in the market.
Under these circumstances, a new draft regulation for direct listings has been framed. This will simplify the pathway for blue-chip companies to enter the capital market while ensuring an expedited processing system.
Stating that efforts are underway to simplify IPO regulations, he mentioned that rules are being revised to encourage issuers to join the market. The revised draft may be published for public consultation within the next two to three weeks.
He informed that listing fees for bonds have been significantly reduced. Additionally, institutions applying for direct listing or IPOs by March 2027 will receive a 50% waiver on listing fees.
He added that the DSE aims to bring at least 10 blue-chip companies to the capital market through direct listing or IPOs by 2027. These entities may include state-owned enterprises, multinationals, and domestic blue-chip corporations.
Highlighting the revision of the country's credit rating outlook from negative to stable as an important signal for the economy, he noted that positive reactions have already been mirrored in the capital market. He expressed hope that the macroeconomic pressures experienced earlier will gradually subside.
To make the capital market more efficient and transparent, the DSE chairman emphasized the need for coordinated efforts among three key institutions: the stock exchange, Central Depository Bangladesh Limited (CDBL), and Central Counterparty Bangladesh Limited (CCBL).

item.title: Savings tools remain safe investment for people
item.description:
Confidence in the banking and stock markets has not fully recovered. Amid this, with the interest rates on National Savings Certificates (Sanchayapatra) remaining temporarily unchanged, savers are once again leaning toward this medium in search of safe investments.
Evidence of this was seen in the sales figures of the first month of the current fiscal year.
In July, net sales of savings certificates reached Tk2,059.47 crore, which is nearly 59% higher than the same period last fiscal year and almost 5 times the net sales of the entire FY26.
Bangladesh Bank's updated report shows that in July 2025, net sales were Tk1,293.48 crore.
Meanwhile, total net sales for the entire FY26 stood at just Tk436 crore.
This means that net sales in a single month were nearly 5 times higher than those of the previous full fiscal year.
On a single-month basis, July’s sales were the highest in four years. Previously, in February 2022, net savings certificate sales reached Tk2,523 crore. Since then, net sales had not crossed Tk2,000 crore in any month.
In fact, net sales were negative for the past three consecutive fiscal years, meaning more money was spent repaying the principal and interest of older certificates than was generated through new sales.
At the end of July, the government's outstanding debt balance through savings certificates rose to Tk336,061.82 crore, up from Tk334,002.35 crore in June.
Net investment in savings certificates is considered government borrowing and is used to cover the budget deficit.
Explaining the sudden surge in interest, economists say that although deposit rates in banks have increased slightly, public confidence in the banking sector has not completely returned.
The stock market has also experienced long-standing uncertainty. Fearing that interest rates on savings certificates might decrease soon, many invested early.
Mustafa K Mujeri, former chief economist of Bangladesh Bank, said that a confidence deficit still persists in the banking sector. Amid inflationary pressures, people are eager to protect whatever small savings they manage to retain by turning to savings certificates.
According to Mujeri, there is no risk of losing capital, it offers easy liquidation if needed, and the return rate remains relatively attractive.
Meanwhile, the government’s borrowing target from savings certificates for the current fiscal year is set at Tk8,500 crore.
However, the government has decided to keep the existing interest rates unchanged for the next six months.
The rule regarding the 10% tax deducted at source has also been revised in the new budget; this tax will no longer be considered a final tax and can now be adjusted in the income tax return.
Stakeholders claim that under these circumstances, the rise in savings certificate sales is not merely a shift in investor preference, but also a message for the government.
Over the past few years, desired borrowing targets from this sector were not met, leading to increased reliance on the banking sector to cover deficits.
If investment in savings certificates continues to rise, it will strengthen the government's alternative borrowing sources.
However, given that people's capacity to save has declined during this period of high inflation, it remains to be seen how sustainable this trend will be.

Travel ban on 4, including ex-Bangladesh envoy to UK
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday imposed a travel ban on four people, including former Bangladesh High Commissioner to the United Kingdom Saida Muna Tasneem and her husband Touhidul Islam Chowdhury, over graft allegations.
The two other people barred by the court from leaving the country are their two sons, Alvi Azfar Chowdhury and Javed Opgenhaffen.
Dhaka Metropolitan Senior Special Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir passed the order, allowing a plea of the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC).
According to the case documents, an investigation is underway against Touhidul Islam Chowdhury, Saida Muna Tasneem and others over allegations of embezzling approximately Taka 2,000 crore in loans from various banks and financial institutions through collusion and corruption, and laundering the money abroad.
“A reliable source revealed during the investigation that the persons concerned might leave the country and flee abroad. Therefore, it was essential to impose a ban on their travel abroad in the interest of a proper investigation,” the ACC plea said.
The same court also imposed a travel ban on Emma Claire Burton, the British-origin wife of former education minister Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury Nowfel, for not submitting a wealth statement.

item.title: Gazi Nazrul’s first wife sent to jail after one-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday sent Maksuda Islam, the first wife of lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam, to jail after a one-day remand in a case filed over the alleged instigation of the suicide of his second wife, Mariam.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ripon Hossain passed the order after Investigation Officer Inspector Mohammad Salauddin of the DB Tejgaon Zonal Team produced Maksuda before the court and sought an order to send her to jail.
The investigation officer told the court that important information related to the case had been obtained during her interrogation and would assist the investigation.
Rafiqul Islam, an SI of the prosecution department, said no bail petition was filed on behalf of Maksuda.
Mariam’s father, SM Masum Billah, filed the case on Sunday night, accusing Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman of instigating her suicide.
Police recovered Mariam’s hanging body from a flat at NAM Bhaban opposite the parliament building on Sunday evening.
Later that night, Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda were taken into custody.
The following day, a court granted four days’ remand for Gazi Nazrul and one day for Maksuda. The investigation was later handed over to the DB.
What the FIR says
According to the FIR, Mariam, 19, married Gazi Nazrul in June under the “direct instigation” of her maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman.
After the marriage, Mariam lived with Nazrul and Maksuda at House 203 of NAM Bhaban opposite the parliament building.
The FIR said, Mariam told her family that Nazrul and Maksuda physically and mentally tortured her over various issues after the marriage.
At around 5:30pm on Sunday, Nazrul called Mariam’s father and asked him to go to the residence quickly. When he arrived, he found his daughter hanging, according to the FIR.
Several handwritten notes were also found on Mariam’s bed, according to the FIR.
The FIR alleged that Mariam wrote about her mental distress, feeling deceived and frustration over a romantic relationship in the notes.
According to the FIR, Mariam may have died by suicide between 3pm and 5:30pm on Sunday.
Gazi Nazrul expelled from Jamaat
The case follows a controversy surrounding Gazi Nazrul and Mariam that began after a video of the two at a hotel in Dhaka’s Moghbazar went viral on social media on the night of July 20.
Jamaat leaders and activists initially claimed that the video had been created using artificial intelligence.
Gazi Nazrul later said in a Facebook post that Mariam was his second wife.
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami subsequently decided to expel him on July 22, saying an organizational investigation had found allegations of moral misconduct to be proven.
The opposition party later informed the speaker and the Election Commission of the decision through letters.

item.title: Zahed defends fuel price hike, outlines govt plans
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Affairs Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday briefed journalists on Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to New York for the UN General Assembly and the government’s ongoing initiatives, while defending the recent fuel price hike.
Dr Zahed Ur Rahman disclosed the plans at the government’s weekly briefing at the Press Information Department (PID) on Tuesday.
He also briefed journalists on the prime minister’s UN visit, Bangladesh’s position on the Rohingya crisis and climate change, and the government’s ongoing activities across several ministries.
Tarique Rahman reached in New York to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, with his official engagements beginning on Tuesday.
He is scheduled to address the General Assembly on September 24, with the Rohingya crisis, climate change, rising sea levels, global inequality, and maternal and newborn health among the issues receiving particular attention during his visit.
Zahed said on September 23, the prime minister is scheduled to attend a high-level meeting on global inequality, a meeting on climate action and just transition, and a side event on the Rohingya crisis jointly hosted by Bangladesh and Gambia.
At the Rohingya event, he will seek international support for the safe and swift repatriation of Rohingyas to Myanmar, Zahed added.
“International attention to the Rohingya issue has declined compared to the past due to various global crises. But the prolonged stay of a large number of Rohingyas in Bangladesh is creating not only economic pressure but also security concerns,” he said.
On the country’s gas situation, Zahed said the major supply crisis seen in August had improved significantly.
Titas Gas Field’s Well No 28 in Brahmanbaria was formally inaugurated on September 19 and is now supplying 12.5 million cubic feet of gas per day to the national grid.
The government plans to drill 150 wells by 2030 to reduce dependence on imported gas, he said.
The plan includes drilling new wells, carrying out workovers of existing wells and conducting two-dimensional and three-dimensional seismic surveys to identify new gas fields.
“Long-term, there are very limited sustainable alternatives to increasing domestic gas exploration and production,” Zahed said.
Defending the recent fuel price increase, Zahed said international oil prices, transportation and insurance costs, and high LNG prices were putting significant financial pressure on the government.
From September 21, diesel prices rose from Tk115 to Tk135 per litre, octane from Tk145 to Tk165, petrol from Tk140 to Tk160 and kerosene from Tk135 to Tk155.
“We do not deny that people will suffer. The government’s job will be to minimize that suffering,” he said.
The government expects the Tk20-per-litre increase to reduce the annual subsidy burden by several thousand crore taka.
Zahed said the government would also monitor the impact of the diesel price increase on transport fares and essential commodity prices.
Asked about plans to increase the salaries of government employees amid substantial subsidy requirements in the fuel and power sectors, Zahed said the government had to balance several priorities.
He said the last national pay scale was introduced in 2015 and that inflation had significantly increased the cost of living over the past decade.
The government is therefore moving towards implementing a new pay structure in phases rather than increasing expenditure all at once, he said.
First electric train planned for Narayanganj-Dhaka-Joydebpur route
The government has taken up a Tk3,822.51 crore project to introduce electric trains on the Narayanganj-Dhaka-Joydebpur route.
The project, already approved by Ecnec, involves installing an electric traction system along around 52km of railway track and procuring electric multiple unit trains, the adviser said.
It is scheduled to be completed by 2031.
Project estimates suggest operating and fuel costs will fall significantly compared with diesel-powered trains, while maintenance costs could decline by 35-40%.
The government will initially prioritize landless and homeless families, families with members with disabilities, members from the hijra and Bede communities, ethnic minority groups and families owning half an acre or less of land under the Family Card program.
Door-to-door data collection and the creation of an integrated database are underway to identify eligible households, Zahed said.
Government employees, pensioners, large business owners and families owning cars, air conditioners or other significant luxury assets will initially not be eligible.
The policy is to issue one Family Card per household.
Airfare for Hajj pilgrims in 2027 has been set at Tk130,000, Tk24,830 lower than the 2026 fare, Zahed said.
He said the government had been gradually reducing Hajj airfares to make the overall cost of the pilgrimage more affordable.
Asked about Tarique Rahman’s scheduled meeting with Boeing Global President Dr Brendan Nelson and whether an agreement would be signed, Zahed said he had no information beyond what had been officially communicated to him.
He said discussions between Bangladesh and Boeing had already been publicly disclosed.
The published schedule for the prime minister’s New York visit includes a meeting with Nelson and a signing ceremony in the presence of Bangladesh government representatives.
The government has also approved the reopening of Nilphamari’s Darowani Textile Mills and Magura Textile Mills through public-private partnerships, Zahed said.
He said 13,949 religious leaders and service workers had already received state honorariums, including imams, muezzins, khadims, priests and Buddhist religious service workers.
Meanwhile, a Ministry of Science and Technology project has completed the collection of marine baseline data from around 20,000sq km of sea area.
The data is expected to help identify potential mineral resources and assess microplastic and other pollution in coastal areas.
A 40-day residential training camp is also being held at Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protishtan for young athletes selected based on their performance in various competitions.

item.title: BLAST demands probe, compensation over Savar explosion
item.description:
Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST) has demanded an urgent and impartial investigation, accountability and adequate compensation following a gas cylinder explosion in Ashulia that left eight people dead and around 25 injured.
The rights organization also called for stronger safety measures to prevent similar incidents involving gas cylinders and other flammable and hazardous substances.
The explosion and subsequent fire occurred at around 6:45pm on Sunday at the industrial premises of Pretty Group in the Jamgora area of Ashulia, Dhaka, involving a vehicle carrying gas cylinders, according to a BLAST press release.
Nearby vehicles and structures were also damaged, it said.
BLAST expressed deep grief over the deaths, conveyed condolences to the families of the victims and wished the injured a speedy recovery.
The organization called for a technical examination of the vehicle involved, gas cylinders, valves, regulators, pipes or hoses, connection systems, and the entire gas transfer and supply system.
It said authorities should verify whether the cylinders and equipment had valid expiry dates, test certificates, registrations and approvals and were fit for use.
BLAST also demanded an investigation into whether the Gas Cylinder Rules, 1991, and other applicable laws and regulations concerning explosives, fire and workplace safety were followed in the transportation, storage, filling, transfer and use of gas cylinders.
It called for verification of whether the factory and related facilities had adequate risk assessments, fire safety measures, emergency response plans, safe loading and unloading arrangements, and systems for managing flammable and pressurized gas.
The organization said authorities should determine whether relevant government agencies and regulatory bodies properly carried out their responsibilities regarding licensing and approvals, regular inspections, safety supervision and enforcement of laws.
If evidence of negligence, carelessness or legal violations by any individual, organization or government official is found, BLAST demanded that accountability be ensured under the law.
It also called for proper assessment of the losses suffered by the families of those killed, the injured and other affected people and demanded adequate compensation.
The organization further demanded that the full cost of necessary medical treatment, long-term care and rehabilitation support for the injured be ensured.
BLAST referred to the 2010 Nimtoli fire and said the High Court had previously considered the responsibilities and accountability of relevant authorities in cases involving fires, flammable and hazardous substances and public safety.

The petition also raised issues concerning strengthening the Fire Service and Civil Defence and providing adequate compensation to those affected, BLAST said.

item.title: Dhaka puts national interest first in UNGA meetings, rules out Trump talks
item.description:
Bangladesh will put its national interests at the centre of more than a dozen bilateral and multilateral engagements on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said, as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman begins his first UNGA visit as head of government.
Kobir also ruled out the possibility of a bilateral meeting between Tarique Rahman and US President Donald Trump during the visit.
“The prime minister has come on this visit to attend the UN session,” the state minister told reporters in response to a question about a possible meeting with Trump.
Tarique arrived in New York on Monday evening local time to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, where he is scheduled to deliver his maiden address as prime minister on September 24.
His visit comes with a packed diplomatic agenda, with more than a dozen bilateral, multilateral and courtesy meetings expected on the sidelines of the UN gathering.
Bangladesh has said the engagements will focus on advancing its diplomatic and economic priorities.
A Turkish Airlines flight carrying the prime minister, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and members of his entourage landed at John F Kennedy International Airport at 6:20pm on Monday local time after a stopover in Istanbul.
Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative to the UN Irene Khan, Ambassador to the United States Tareq Md Ariful Islam and Deputy Permanent Representative AKM Wahiduzzaman received Tarique and Zubaida at the VIP lounge of Terminal 1.
After completing airport formalities, the prime minister was taken in a motorcade to the Hyatt Grand Central New York, where he will stay during the visit.
Tarique left Dhaka early Monday morning accompanied by his wife and a high-level delegation that includes ministers, state ministers, senior government officials and advisers.
His official engagements are set to begin on Tuesday with a welcome breakfast hosted by UN Secretary-General António Guterres for heads of state and government.
He is also scheduled to attend the opening of the UNGA session and a reception hosted by the US president for visiting heads of state and government and their spouses.
The centrepiece of the visit will be Tarique’s first address to the UN General Assembly as prime minister on September 24.
His speech is expected to set out Bangladesh’s positions on its democratic transition, rule of law and accountability, global peace and security, climate change, sustainable development, economic cooperation, the Rohingya crisis and reform of the multilateral system.
The visit marks the incumbent government’s first appearance at the United Nations’ highest-level annual gathering since taking office.

item.title: Welfare fee increased for Bangladeshi migrant workers
item.description:
The government has increased the welfare fee for Bangladeshi workers going abroad by Tk2,000, raising it from Tk3,500 to Tk5,500.
The revised fee will come into effect on October 1, according to a circular issued by the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment.
Workers going abroad are required to become members of the Wage Earners’ Welfare Board by paying the fee before departure.
The circular, signed by the ministry’s Senior Assistant Secretary Saiyeda Faizunnesa, said the fee was revised to ensure the overall welfare and protection of migrant workers as the scope and volume of services provided to them have increased.
The ministry also said the fee was adjusted in line with the current exchange rate and market prices.
The Tk5,500 welfare fee will apply to fees collected from workers going abroad, those already overseas and workers from whom the fee is collected at airports.
