item.title: Noakhali man arrested for raping fifth-grader
item.description:
Police on Saturday arrested a man for raping a fifth-grade student from Sharifpur union, Noakhali
The arrestee has been identified as Alamgir Hossain Forazi, 45. He previously served as the Jamaat-e-Islami secretary of Ward 4 of Sharifpur union in the district.
Begumganj Model police station Officer-in-Charge Shamsuzzaman confirmed the matter on Sunday afternoon.
According to the complaint, the rape survivor went to a medicine shop on the evening of September 13 after developing a headache. Alamgir, who runs the shop, also allegedly practises traditional healing.
In the complaint, the child’s father said Alamgir took the child to a room behind the shop, claiming the headache could be cured through a ritual. The child was raped there and threatened with death if he disclosed the incident.
Later, when the child complained of pain, family members questioned him. At one point, he told them the details of the incident.
Sharifpur union Jamaat secretary Mozammel Hossain said: “Alamgir served in Jamaat’s Ward 4 until 2022. He is currently inactive and is not involved in any party activities.”
Begumganj Model police station Officer-in-Charge Shamsuzzaman said the child’s father filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000 on Saturday night. Alamgir was arrested that night in connection with the case and was sent to a judicial court on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Four KU students sued over NWU student’s death in Khulna
item.description:
A murder case has been filed against four students of Khulna University (KU) and 20-25 other unidentified people over the death of North Western University (NWU) student Md Azmal Hossain in Khulna.
Qutb Uddin, father of the victim, filed the case with Harintana Police Station around 10:00pm on Saturday, said its Officer-in-Charge Md Iqbal Hossain.
However, the names of the four KU students could not be known immediately.
According to the case statement, Azmal was beaten at a mess on Masjid Goli of Islamnagar Road, opposite the Khan Jahan Ali Hall of KU, after being accused of theft on Friday night. At one stage, he fell from the roof of the four-storey building.
He was taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital in critical condition around 1:30am on Saturday, where he died.
Police and local sources said Azmal, a first-year student of the English Department at NWU situated at Sonadanga, ate at the mess on Friday night without paying for the meal, which allegedly led to an altercation.
Several students of the mess and some locals later accused him of theft and allegedly beat him.
He was subsequently taken to the rooftop, where he was allegedly beaten further. His hair was also cut.
Azmal hailed from Bara Sholua village under Darshana Police Station in Chuadanga and lived in a rented mess in the Masjid Goli area near KU.
Azmal’s family also alleged that someone called them during the incident and demanded Tk 100,000. The phone was later found to be switched off. Police said they were investigating the allegation.
“We are investigating the incident and will take legal action against those found to be involved,” said OC Iqbal Hossain.
He said four KU students were named in the case, while another 20-25 unidentified people were also accused.

item.title: Three people, including freedom fighter, killed in Gopalganj road crashes
item.description:
Three people, including a freedom fighter, killed in separate bus crashes in Kashiani upazila of Gopalganj on late Saturday night and Sunday.
The first accident occurred in the Panchabatti area of the Dhaka-Khulna highway.
The deceased were identified as Omar Mir, 75, a freedom fighter and Jahid Molla, 50, both residents of the area.
Locals said Omar and Jahid were walking along the highway when a bus hit them, leaving both critically injured. Omar was rushed to Muksudpur Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead. Jahid died at the scene.
Sub Inspector Obaidul Kazi of Bhanga Highway Police Station confirmed the deaths. He said police visited the scene, prepared inquest reports and handed over the bodies to the families after completing legal procedures.
In another accident on the same highway early Sunday, a human hauler driver was killed after an unidentified bus rammed the vehicle in the Fokra bus stand area of Kashiani around 4am.
The impact crushed the human haular, killing the driver on the spot.
Rokonuzzaman, officer-in-charge of Bhatiapara Highway Police Station, confirmed the incident and said police recovered the body and sent it to a hospital morgue for autopsy.
The identities of the driver and the bus involved could not immediately be ascertained as the accident occurred before dawn. Police are working to identify the deceased and locate the bus.

item.title: Students withdraw Dhaka-Chittagong highway blockade
item.description:
Students of Comilla University and other educational institutions have withdrawn their blockade of the Dhaka-Chittagong highway after announcing a four-point list of demands, with traffic movement gradually returning to normal.
The students began the blockade in the Kotbari area of Comilla on Sunday afternoon, demanding justice for the murder of 13-year-old Ishayat Shahriar Opratim.
They cleared the highway around 12:30pm after holding a protest procession from the university’s main gate following Opratim’s namaz-e-janaza on campus.
The procession moved towards the Kotbari intersection, where the students blocked the Dhaka-Chittagong highway.
Their four demands are: the arrest of those involved in Opratim’s murder within 12 hours and a guarantee of a speedy trial; an acknowledgement of failure in handling the murder case from the Comilla superintendent of police and the police forces of Kotwali Model Police Station and Sadar Dakshin Police Station; the establishment of a permanent police outpost in the university area; and visible measures to improve the law and order situation in Comilla.

item.title: Call to halt NCT lease process to DP World
item.description:
Chattogram Bandar Rakkha Parishad has demanded that the government halt the ongoing process to lease the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) at Chittagong Port to foreign operator DP World.
At a press conference organised at the Chittagong Press Club on yesterday, the parishad gave the government two days to meet its four-point demands, warning of a series of protest programs otherwise.
The demands include scrapping the lease process, withdrawing cases filed against port leaders and 15 employees over previous protests, removing port officials involved in the proposed agreement with DP World, and filling vacant posts at the port.
Joint Coordinator Humayun Kabir alleged that successive governments had attempted to hand over NCT to DP World since 2017, despite concerns over national interests. He said the interim government also continued the process after August 5, 2024, but later stepped back following protests by the parishad, labour organisations and professionals.
The parishad also rejected claims by the port chairman that NCT’s equipment was outdated and operating at only 70% capacity. It said port documents, equipment procurement records and assessments by maritime logistics experts did not support the claim.
It also warned that leasing NCT to DP World could create economic and security risks, including job losses and increased pressure on foreign exchange. It claimed NCT generated about Tk4,500 crore in revenue in the 2025-26 fiscal year, including Tk2,500 crore in net income.
The parishad announced a human chain on September 22 and a protest procession on September 27 if its demands are not met.

item.title: Gopalganj achieves Boro procurement target
item.description:
Gopalganj has achieved its target for paddy and rice procurement under the government’s Boro-2026 procurement programme, with paddy collection already completed and rice procurement continuing for mills that received additional allocations.
Gopalganj District Food Controller Anik Pal Ontu said the Ministry of Food had set a target of procuring 14,583 tonnes of paddy, 14,076 tonnes of parboiled rice and 242 tonnes of atap rice from six government food warehouses in the district.
The government fixed the procurement price at Tk 36 per kilogram for paddy and Tk 49 per kilogram for rice.
“We started the procurement campaign in May and completed paddy procurement well ahead of the deadline,” Anik Pal said.
So far, 14,318 tonnes of rice, including parboiled and atap rice, have been procured. Additional allocations were later given to some rice mills following applications from mill owners, and procurement from those mills is still continuing, he said.
The six government warehouses in Gopalganj have a combined storage capacity of 14,950 tonnes after a 30 per cent increase in capacity. Against this, the district has already procured 28,901 tonnes of paddy and rice—14,311 tonnes more than the warehouses can accommodate.
The additional stocks have been transported to government warehouses with available capacity in Faridpur, Rajbari, the Narayanganj silo, the Mongla silo and other locations, the district food controller said.
Paddy was procured directly from farmers, with each farmer allowed to sell up to three tonnes at Tk 36 per kilogram. Payments were made directly to farmers’ bank accounts.
“ We did not allow any syndicate to become active in the paddy procurement process,” Anik Pal said.
However, farmers and agricultural officials said government procurement covers only a small portion of the district’s total production.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Boro rice was cultivated on 82,593 hectares in Gopalganj this year, slightly above the target of 82,588 hectares.
The district’s production target was 635,927 tonnes, but actual production reached 646,703 tonnes—10,776 tonnes above the target.
Sanjay Kumar Kundu, acting deputy director of the DAE’s Gopalganj office, estimated that around 17,000 farmers may be involved in Boro cultivation in the district.
“According to the Directorate General of Food, paddy has been procured from around 5,000 farmers. This needs to be increased. If government procurement is expanded, it will encourage farmers to increase cultivation and production,” he said.
The government procurement price was higher than the prevailing market price, benefiting farmers who were able to sell their produce to government warehouses.
Parimal Biswas, a farmer from Charpara village in Raghunathpur Union, said he sold three tonnes of paddy at Tk 36 per kilogram.
“I am very happy to sell my paddy to the government. If the government continues buying from farmers this way, we will benefit,” he said.
Parimal said he produced 12 tonnes of paddy this year and urged the government to increase the maximum procurement limit from three tonnes to six tonnes per farmer.
But farmer Majed Sardar of Khanarpar village in Kathi Union said he produced 21 tonnes of paddy but could not sell any to the government.
“I was forced to sell my paddy to traders at Tk 1,000 per maund. I am disappointed. I want to sell my paddy to the government, so the procurement allocation in Gopalganj should be increased,” he said.
Md Momin Khan, an assistant professor in the Department of Food Science at Gopalganj Science and Technology University, called for increased government procurement, farmer support and expansion of storage facilities.
Nearly 650,000 tonnes of paddy were produced in Gopalganj this season, while the government’s paddy procurement target was only 14,583 tonnes, he noted.
“The amount procured from farmers is very small compared with total production,” he said.
Momin Khan also called for the construction of more government food warehouses so that larger stocks could be maintained for emergencies.
“More paddy should be procured directly from farmers. At the same time, new government warehouses should be built to increase storage capacity,” he said.
He also urged the authorities to curb the influence of intermediaries and ensure fair prices for farmers, saying stronger procurement and storage capacity would help reinforce food security.

item.title: Titumir: Global financial architecture must create conditions for sustainable development
item.description:
Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, adviser to the prime minister on the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Planning, has called for comprehensive reform of the global financial architecture to ensure affordable, predictable and vulnerability-sensitive financing for developing countries.
Speaking at the Leaders' Dialogue on “Leading SDG Action” during the 2026 SDG Moment, convened by the UN Secretary-General at the UN General Assembly Hall in New York, Titumir said, "Our broader vision should be collective and forward-looking: a global financial architecture that does not merely finance development, but creates the conditions in which development can be sustained."
He outlined five priorities for reforming the international financial architecture, particularly for multilateral development banks: shifting from crisis response to anticipating vulnerabilities; giving vulnerable countries a stronger voice in international financial institutions; providing longer-term, lower-cost and predictable finance; aligning international finance with national development strategies through coordinated, multi-year financing; and ensuring flexible transition support and preferential arrangements for LDC-graduating countries, including Bangladesh.
He also highlighted Bangladesh's SDG Village initiative as an integrated, community-led approach to translating the SDGs into tangible improvements at the local level, said a press release of the Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations.
The dialogue also featured Teresa Ribera of the European Commission, Aristide M‚d‚nou, Minister of Economy and Finance of Benin, and Beatriz Carles de Arango, Minister for Social Development of Panama.
Sherwin Bryce-Pease of the South African Broadcasting Corporation moderated the discussion.

item.title: Farmgate secret meeting: 12 placed on 3-day remand over suspected militant links
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Saturday placed 12 people, arrested over suspected militant activities during a secret meeting at Tejgaon College Jame Mosque in Farmgate, on three-day remand.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Arifur Rahman passed the order after a hearing on Saturday. Earlier, CTTC Inspector Akhter Morshed, the investigating officer in the case, sought seven days’ remand for each of the accused. Public prosecutor Azizul Haque Didar confirmed the matter.
During the hearing, the prosecution said the accused had allegedly planned to create instability in the country and recruit people to carry out jihad. Their remand was necessary to identify others involved, the prosecution said.
Defence lawyer Masud-ur Rahman opposed the remand plea and sought bail for the accused.
According to the remand application, the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit learned through intelligence and information technology that several young men had gathered near the Tejgaon Coca-Cola intersection with plans to disrupt public order, spread extremism and carry out a major violent incident.
Police later conducted a raid on May 18 with assistance from Tejgaon and Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police and arrested them.
Police said the arrestees were members of a secret WhatsApp group called “Meetup”, through which they allegedly exchanged extremist messages and communicated on various issues. Investigators alleged that they had gathered to plan subversive activities.
The arrested individuals are Mohammad Shihab Uddin, 32; Marzuk Ahmed, 26; Saifur Rahman Khan, 32; Rashmi Mia, 29; Kamichul Islam, 36; Sajjad Hossain, 22; Afif Ahmed, 20; Mohaiminul Haque, 27; Zauji Chowdhury, 19; Shahadat Hossain, 25; Sakib Ahmed, 26; and Junaid Ahmed, 21.
The CTTC said Shihab Uddin had previously been accused of involvement in extremist activities. A case filed against him under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Palash Police Station in Narsingdi is pending trial. Marzuk Ahmed is also facing a pending case under the Speedy Trial Act with Tejgaon police station.
The investigating officer said the accused needed to be questioned to ensure a proper investigation and uncover the circumstances surrounding the incident.The remand application also sought to recover and examine their mobile phones, SIM cards and other digital evidence, as well as analyse cyber data.
Investigators said they also needed to verify the suspects’ communications on WhatsApp, Facebook, Telegram, Messenger and other social media platforms, identify the alleged planners and accomplices, and trace the sources of funding and financiers of the suspected extremist activities.
The court rejected the bail pleas and granted three days’ remand for each of the 12 accused.

item.title: Saudi capital issues first air raid alert since renewed fighting in Yemen
item.description:
Explosions were heard in Riyadh early Saturday, AFP journalists reported, after Saudi authorities issued their first air raid alert in the capital since fighting returned to neighboring Yemen.
The Houthis have been fighting with Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces since the country’s civil war reignited in July, when the group also declared a maritime blockade on Riyadh and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea.
This is the first time the conflict has reached the capital, further shaking a global economy already rattled by nearly seven months of war between the United States and Iran.
“The area is under a hostile aerial threat,” a message received shortly before 3am (0000 GMT) by residents of the Saudi capital warned, urging them to stay indoors.
AFP journalists then heard two explosions, before the alert was lifted about half an hour later by Saudi Arabia’s civil defense agency.
Saudi Arabia is yet to comment on the threat mentioned in the warnings sent overnight to residents of several regions and has not identified where it originated from.
It comes after Riyadh accused the group of targeting Mecca on Wednesday, denouncing it as a “cowardly terrorist attack” on Islam’s holy city, which welcomes millions of pilgrims each year, both Sunnis and Shias.
The Houthis strongly denied the accusation calling it a “worn-out lie.”
In turn, the group reported dozens of retaliatory strikes carried out daily by Riyadh since their lightning offensive this month to take over the country’s entire Red Sea coast, giving them control over the vital Bab al-Mandab strait.
The war in Yemen broke out in 2014 when the Houthis seized control of the capital Sanaa and other regions, triggering in March 2015 a military intervention led by Saudi Arabia.
The fragile truce reached in 2022 between the warring parties collapsed in July, when the pro-Iranian fighters defied Riyadh’s control of Yemeni airspace by allowing an Iranian aircraft to land in Yemen.
Their recent takeover of the coastline has sparked global concern, with international maritime trade already heavily impacted by Tehran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the Middle East war in late February.
The Houthis, for their part, insist there is no threat to shipping in the sea lane -- except for Saudi ships, from the world’s leading crude exporter.
Figures from maritime tracking firm Kpler showed that Saudi exports via the Bab al-Mandab strait had dropped since July, although five loaded ships had passed through in the last week.
The United States, which according to Axios last week refused to strike the Houthis at Saudi Arabia’s request, approved the sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to the kingdom on Thursday.
The sale, worth $24.3 billion, is intended to help Riyadh “deter current and future threats,” the US State Department said.
The UN said Friday that the renewed fighting had displaced more than 112,000 people while nearly 3,000 others had fled across the sea to Djibouti, heaping further misery on an already struggling population.

item.title: Girl gang-raped in Kushtia dies at RMCH after 4 days
item.description:
A 20-year-old girl who was reportedly raped by four people on Thursday died at Rajshahi Medical College and Hospital early Saturday.
The deceased was a resident of Bheramara upazila of Kushtia district.
Rafiqul Islam, Officer-in-Charge of Bheramara Police Station, said mother of the girl lodged a complaint with the police station.
According to the complaint, a motorcycle waylaid Toma at Gopalnagar around 9pm on Thursday and picked her up to an abandoned place when she was returning to her home in Fakirabad Bakshipara.
Later, four people raped her, and all the accused left the place after leaving her at Bakshipara around 12am.
Around 12:30am, family members of Toma rescued her and took her to Bheramara Upazila Health Complex.
She was then referred to Rajshahi Medical College and Hospital, where she succumbed to her injuries around 2:30am on Saturday.
Family members of the girl claimed that she got divorced from her husband, Abu Bakkar, one and a half months ago, and her ex-husband might have been involved in the abduction and rape.
However, police detained Abu Bakkar in this connection.

item.title: DSCC plans to produce electricity, gas, compost, diesel from recycled waste
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Md Abdus Salam has said plans are underway to recycle waste to produce electricity, gas, compost fertilizer and diesel.
He made the remarks as the chief guest at the inauguration of a “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” at Swarighat on the Buriganga River in Dhaka on Saturday. The program was jointly organized by Bidyanondo Foundation and DSCC.
Abdus Salam said waste should not simply be viewed as garbage but should instead be converted into a resource.
“We are focusing on how we can quickly generate electricity through waste recycling. We believe we will be able to move to the initial stage in this regard within a few months,” he said.
“Then waste will be transformed into a resource. It will no longer be left scattered everywhere. On the one hand, we need to raise public awareness, and on the other, we need to recycle waste to produce electricity, gas, compost fertilizer and diesel. Our activities in this regard are already underway,” he added.
The DSCC administrator said the Buriganga was once the lifeline of Dhaka, but plastic, polythene and other waste now float in the river.
He said the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative had been launched to raise public awareness about preventing river and environmental pollution and to promote the idea of treating waste as a resource.
“We know that all the problems of the Buriganga will not be solved through today’s initiative. But it will send a message to the public that we want to do this and that we need to do it,” he said.
Calling on citizens to come forward to protect the Buriganga, Abdus Salam said people living along both banks of the river and those conducting businesses dependent on it also had a responsibility to act responsibly.
“The Buriganga has reached a point where failure to protect it will leave a bleak future,” he said.
He said initiatives were also being taken to make the Dhaleshwari, Shitalakkhya, Balu and Turag rivers surrounding Dhaka navigable.
“Necessary steps will be taken to restore the river-based transport system that previously connected Dhaka,” he said.
Abdus Salam said under the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative, plastic and other waste collected from the river and its banks would be accepted through a designated process.
He said there were plans to gradually expand the initiative to all 75 wards under DSCC.
He added that efforts were underway to launch a pilot project in Kamrangirchar in coordination with Bidyanondo Foundation. The project would explore how waste could be recycled and converted into usable resources.
The DSCC administrator also urged citizens to remain vigilant to prevent dengue.
“Dengue cannot be prevented through city corporation activities alone. Coconut shells, water from air conditioners, stagnant water on rooftops or water accumulating anywhere else must not be allowed to remain. If breeding grounds for mosquitoes can be destroyed, dengue can be prevented to a large extent,” he said.
Speaking as a special guest, Dhaka-7 MP Hamidur Rahman said the initiative primarily aimed to encourage people to collect plastic and other waste lying in and around the river.
“Providing food and essential goods in exchange for waste will raise environmental awareness while also promoting the idea of treating waste as a reusable resource,” he said.
He said the initiative should be continued regularly by involving low-income people living along the river.
“If a designated waste collection point and office are established, it will be possible to collect waste while also meeting the food and essential-goods needs of low-income people,” he added.
Under the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative, people can exchange collected waste, after it is weighed, for various essential goods, including rice, lentils, flour, cooking oil, fish, chicken and noodles.

item.title: Dhaka air quality turns ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 13th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Saturday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 121 at 9:02am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups”, posing health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Pakistan’s Lahore, India’s Kolkata and Malaysia’s Kuching occupied the first three spots on list with AQI scores of 179, 171 and 169, respectively.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is categorized as "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.
